definition_zh: 再次发生；重现；重提；（小数）循环
definition_en: to happen again, to come back to mind or to a subject, or of a decimal, to repeat endlessly
core_image: 入冬之后，同一间候诊室里又坐满同样咳嗽的人
scene: 每年入冬，镇上那家诊所的候诊室里又坐满同样咳嗽的人。 The same cough recurs in the clinic every winter.
sceneCN: 这里 recur 指再次发生（第 1 个义项：同一件事在一段时间之后重来）；句意为每年入冬，那家诊所里同样的咳嗽又出现。

pos.zh: 再次发生；重现；重提；循环

senses.title: A problem that recurs
senses.definition: of an event or condition, to happen again after an interval
senses.definitionCN: 指事件或状况隔一段时间再次发生
senses.example: The same cough recurs in the clinic every winter.
senses.exampleCN: 每年冬天，同样的咳嗽都会在那家诊所里出现。
senses.why: The first sense is about time: the same thing returns on a schedule or a cycle.
senses.whyCN: 第一个义项讲的是时间：同一件事按周期回来。

senses.title: A memory that recurs
senses.definition: of a thought, image or symptom, to come back to the mind or body
senses.definitionCN: 指念头、画面或症状重新回到心里或身上
senses.example: The same image recurred to her at the sound of a door closing.
senses.exampleCN: 门一响，同一个画面又回到她脑海里。
senses.why: Here the return is inward, inside one person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的返回是向内的，发生在一个人心里。

senses.title: To recur to a subject
senses.definition: to return in speech or writing to an earlier point
senses.definitionCN: 在说话或写作中回到先前的一点
senses.example: Let us recur to the question of cost before we go on.
senses.exampleCN: 在继续之前，让我们回到成本这个问题。
senses.why: The verb can mean a speaker going back, not an event.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以指说话人往回走，而不是事件重来。

senses.title: A decimal that recurs
senses.definition: of a decimal, to repeat the same digits without end
senses.definitionCN: 指小数位上的同一串数字无限重复
senses.example: The decimal recurs after the third digit.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小数在第三位之后开始循环。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for a pattern that never stops.
senses.whyCN: 数学用这个词指一种永不停止的模式。

intro.en: Recur comes from Latin recurrere, 'to run back', from re- and currere, 'to run'.
intro.cn: recur 来自拉丁语 recurrere（跑回来），由 re- 加 currere（跑）构成。

items.en: Currere meant to run.
items.cn: currere 意为跑。

items.en: The compound meant to run back or return.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为跑回来、返回。

items.en: English used it for events that come round again.
items.cn: 英语用它指再度到来事件。

items.en: Doctors used it for symptoms that return.
items.cn: 医生用它说回来的症状。

items.en: Arithmetic gave it the sense of a repeating decimal.
items.cn: 算术给了它循环小数的意义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the recur- family and its near spellings; the near-meaning group separates repeat, reappear, persist and return.
note.cn: 形近组是 recur 词族及其相近拼写；近义组把「重复」「再现」「持续」「返回」分开。

entries.definition: a return of the same event.
entries.definitionCN: 同一事件的回归。

entries.definition: happening repeatedly.
entries.definitionCN: 反复发生的。

entries.definition: a turning to help.
entries.definitionCN: 求助；追索权。

entries.definition: defined by referring to itself.
entries.definitionCN: 以自我指涉定义的。

entries.definition: to do or say the same thing again.
entries.definitionCN: 再做或再说同一件事。

entries.definition: to come into sight again.
entries.definitionCN: 重新出现在视野中。

entries.definition: to continue without stopping.
entries.definitionCN: 不停地持续下去。

entries.definition: to come back to a place or state.
entries.definitionCN: 回到某个地方或状态。

normalIntro.en: The hooks keep the picture of the same coughing patients filling the same waiting room each winter.
normalIntro.cn: 以下联想留住「每年冬天同一间候诊室又坐满同样咳嗽的人」的画面。

normal.en: Recur is re plus cur, to run back: time runs the same way again.
normal.cn: recur 是 re 加 cur，跑回来：时间又按原路跑一遍。

normal.en: Picture the calendar page turning to the same month.
normal.cn: 想象日历又翻到同一个月份。

normal.en: Say rih-KUR; the vowel is the same as in occur.
normal.cn: 读 rih-KUR，元音与 occur 相同。

normal.en: The word needs an interval: recurrence is not mere repetition.
normal.cn: 这个词需要一段间隔：复发不是单纯的重复。

normal.en: Ask how long the gap is, not only that it happens again.
normal.cn: 问间隔有多长，而不只是会不会再来。

abstract.en: To recur is to prove that time has a fold in it.
abstract.cn: 复发就是证明时间里有一道褶。

abstract.en: A recurring problem is a problem that was never quite closed.
abstract.cn: 反复出现的问题，是从未被真正结清的问题。

abstract.en: The word links calendars, memories and decimals in one motion.
abstract.cn: 这个词把日历、记忆与小数连在同一种运动里。

examples.en: The same cough recurs in the clinic every winter.
examples.cn: 每年冬天，同样的咳嗽都会在那家诊所里出现。

examples.en: The same image recurred to her at the sound of a door closing.
examples.cn: 门一响，同一个画面又回到她脑海里。

examples.en: Let us recur to the question of cost before we go on.
examples.cn: 在继续之前，让我们回到成本这个问题。

root: 拉丁语 recurrere（跑回来）→ re- + currere（跑）

sensesIntro.en: Four senses return in four ways: an event in time, an image in the mind, a speaker to a topic, and digits in a decimal.

branches.en: An event returning after an interval.

branches.en: A speaker returning to an earlier point.
branches.cn: 说话人回到先前的一点。

branches.en: Digits returning without end.

branches.en: Both are patterns that refuse to stop.

intro.cn: recur 词族讲的是跑回来：recur、recurrence、recurrent、recursion 共享那个表示「跑」的拉丁动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin currere, 'to run', yields recurrere, 'to run back'; English shortened it to recur and kept the sense of return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 currere（跑）生出 recurrere（跑回来）；英语简化为 recur，保留了「返回」的意思。

definition_zh: n. 默许，纵容；共谋，暗中配合
definition_en: the act of letting wrong doing pass, often on purpose
core_image: 看守者把眼睛转向别处，钥匙却留在原地
scene: 在他的上司默许之下，走私一直没人查。 The smuggling went on with the connivance of his superiors.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：connivance 指默许；句意是在上司默许下走私一直持续。

pos.zh: 默许；共谋

senses.title: A deliberate blind eye
senses.definition: the act of letting a wrong continue without objecting
senses.definitionCN: 不发异议地让错误持续下去
senses.example: The guard acted with the connivance of his superiors.
senses.exampleCN: 看守在上级默许下行事。
senses.why: Latin connivere means to close the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 connivere 意为闭上眼。

senses.title: Quiet partnership in wrong
senses.definition: secret help given to a wrong plan
senses.definitionCN: 暗中给错误计划提供帮助
senses.example: Their connivance let the fraud go on for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的暗中配合让骗局持续多年。
senses.why: The closed eye becomes an open hand.
senses.whyCN: 闭上的眼变成伸出的手。

intro.en: Connivance comes from Latin connivere, to close the eyes.
intro.cn: connivance 源自拉丁语 connivere，意为闭上眼睛。

items.en: Nictare means to blink.
items.cn: nictare 意为眨眼。

items.en: Connivere means to close the eyes or wink.
items.cn: connivere 意为闭眼或眨眼。

items.en: Conniventia names the closed eye.
items.cn: conniventia 指闭眼。

items.en: English used it of winking at faults.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语用它指对过错睁一只眼。

items.en: Law named silent permission connivance.
items.cn: 十九世纪法律把默许称作 connivance。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the conniv- shape; the near-meaning group names shared guilt.
note.cn: 形近组共享 conniv- 形；近义组列出共同过错。

entries.definition: To let wrong pass on purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 有意放过错误。

entries.definition: Quietly scheming or allowing.
entries.definitionCN: 暗中谋划或默许的。

entries.definition: To make someone believe.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人相信。

entries.definition: Involvement in another wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 参与他人的过错。

entries.definition: Secret cooperation to deceive.
entries.definitionCN: 为欺骗而暗中合作。

entries.definition: Acceptance without protest.
entries.definitionCN: 不加反对的接受。

entries.definition: The act of allowing too much.
entries.definitionCN: 过度放任。

normalIntro.en: Connivance is a closed eye that becomes consent.
normalIntro.cn: connivance 是闭上的眼变成了同意。

normal.en: Connivere means to close the eyes.

normal.en: A closed eye lets a fault pass.

normal.en: Connivance is that closed eye.

abstract.en: A guard turning his back to a gate.
abstract.cn: 转身背对大门的一名守卫。

abstract.en: A wink passing across a room.
abstract.cn: 越过房间传递的一个眼色。

abstract.en: A door left unlocked on purpose.
abstract.cn: 故意没锁的门。

examples.en: The deal was done with official connivance.
examples.cn: 这笔交易在官方默许下完成。

examples.en: His connivance made the theft possible.
examples.cn: 他的纵容使盗窃成为可能。

examples.cn: 纵容欺凌会伤害一所学校。

sensesIntro.cn: 先闭眼放过的错，继而被顺手帮了一把。

definition_zh: 把……归类；分门别类整理；判定为某一类；（计算机）自动分类
definition_en: to place something into a class or group according to its features
core_image: 一张张卡片被手指按颜色推进不同的抽屉，抽屉外面贴着写好的字样。
scene: 图书馆新到的书堆在推车上，管理员按主题把它们一本本插进不同的书架。 Librarians categorize new arrivals by subject before they reach the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 categorize 指「按特征把事物归入某一类别」（第 1 个义项：把某一项放进共有特征相同的组里）；句意为管理员在新书入架之前按学科把它们归类。可辨识物件：推车、书脊、书架、主题标签。

pos.zh: 把……归类；把……分门别类
进行归类（较少用）

senses.title: Place an item in a class
senses.titleCN: 把某一项放进某个类别
senses.definition: to decide which class or group an item belongs to and put it there
senses.definitionCN: 判定某一项属于哪个类别或组别，并把它放进去
senses.example: Librarians categorize new arrivals by subject before they reach the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员在新书入架之前按学科把它们归类。
senses.why: The verb is the doing of category: it takes a single item and gives it a home among others like it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词就是「做类别」：拿一个单项，为它在同类中安置一个位置。

senses.title: Sort a whole set into groups
senses.titleCN: 把一整批东西分门别类
senses.definition: to divide a collection into groups so that each group holds one kind
senses.definitionCN: 把一整批东西分开，使每一组只装一种
senses.example: She categorized the photographs by decade and then by place.
senses.exampleCN: 她先按年代、再按地点把照片分门别类。
senses.why: With a plural object the verb describes repeated placing, so the result is a sorted set rather than one assigned item.
senses.whyCN: 宾语为复数时，这个动词描述反复放置的动作，结果是一整套被分好的东西，而不是单项的归属。

senses.title: Judge something to be of a type
senses.definition: to regard or label something as belonging to a particular kind, often with a judgement attached
senses.definitionCN: 把某物看作或标为属于某一特定种类，常带有判断色彩
senses.example: The reviewer categorized the film as a comedy, though it ends in grief.
senses.exampleCN: 评论者把这部电影归为喜剧，尽管它以悲痛收场。
senses.why: The phrase with as shifts the verb from moving an object to declaring its identity, a common pattern with verbs of naming.
senses.whyCN: 与表示「作为」的词连用时，动词从搬运物件转为宣布其身份，这是命名类动词的常见模式。

senses.title: Sort data by machine
senses.definition: to assign records, images or messages to predefined classes by algorithm
senses.definitionCN: 用算法把记录、图像或信息指派到预先设定的类别
senses.example: The filter categorizes every email as work, family or junk.
senses.exampleCN: 过滤器把每封邮件归为工作、家庭或垃圾三类。
senses.why: Computing keeps the clerk's gesture but replaces the hand with a rule, so the verb needs no human subject.
senses.whyCN: 计算机保留了管理员的手势，却用规则代替了手，因此这个动词不必有人的主语。

senses.title: Group experiences in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在认知上把经验归为一类
senses.definition: to treat similar perceptions or memories as instances of one mental kind
senses.definitionCN: 把相似的知觉或记忆当作同一种心理类别中的实例
senses.example: The brain categorizes a new shape in less time than a blink.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑给一个新形状归类的时间比一次眨眼还短。
senses.why: The mind performs the same act invisibly, and the verb is used for it because the outcome is still a class.
senses.whyCN: 心智在看不见的地方做同样的动作，动词仍可用于它，因为结果同样是一个类别。

senses.title: Assign an organism to a taxon
senses.titleCN: 把生物归入某个分类单元
senses.definition: to place an organism or fossil into a taxonomic group on formal grounds
senses.definitionCN: 依据正式标准把生物或化石归入某个分类学类群
senses.example: The team categorized the fossil as an early reptile rather than an amphibian.
senses.exampleCN: 研究团队把这块化石归为早期爬行动物，而不是两栖动物。
senses.why: Taxonomy makes the everyday verb accountable: the box must be justified by shared ancestry or structure.
senses.whyCN: 分类学让这个日常动词负有责任：把东西放进哪个盒子，必须由共同祖先或结构来证明。

senses.title: Put a person into a narrow box
senses.titleCN: 把人简单化地归入某一类
senses.definition: to treat someone chiefly as a member of a broad social group, ignoring individual differences
senses.definitionCN: 主要把某人当作某个宽泛社会群体的成员，忽略个体差异
senses.example: It is unfair to categorize a student by a single test score.
senses.exampleCN: 凭一次考试分数就把一个学生归类是不公平的。
senses.why: The verb's neutral meaning turns critical here because the class replaces the person's particular case.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词的中性含义在这里带上了批评，因为类别取代了此人的具体情形。

senses.title: File records under headings
senses.definition: to store documents or accounts under fixed headings for later retrieval
senses.definitionCN: 把文件或账目按固定类目存放，以便日后检索
senses.example: The accountant categorized each receipt before closing the month.
senses.exampleCN: 会计在结账前把每张收据按类目归档。
senses.why: Filing is the practical form of the same act: an item is put where its kind is kept.
senses.whyCN: 归档是同一动作的实务形式：把一项放到它那一类该在的位置。

intro.en: Categorize is an English verb made from the noun category in the early eighteenth century, on the model of verbs ending in -ize.
intro.cn: categorize 是十八世纪初由名词 category 按动词后缀的构词模式造出的英语动词。

items.en: The Greek noun meant a public statement or accusation, from kata, against, and agoreuein, to speak publicly; the speaking root is generally linked to agora, an assembly.
items.cn: 这个希腊名词指公开陈述或指控，由表示「针对」的成分与「公开说话」的动词构成；说话词根一般被认为与「集会」有关。

items.en: Aristotle's use of its plural for classes of predication gave the word the sense of a class or group that it still carries.
items.cn: 亚里士多德用它指谓述的各类别，赋予这个词「类别、组别」的含义，这一含义沿用至今。

items.en: Latin categoria and French catégorie carried the noun into English as category in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 拉丁 categoria 与法语 catégorie 把这个名词带进英语，十五世纪时写作 category。

items.en: Category plus -ize produced categorize, first recorded in the early eighteenth century, at a time when many learned verbs were being coined this way.
items.cn: category 加动词后缀构成 categorize，最早记录于十八世纪初，当时许多学术动词正是这样造出。

items.en: The verb was later applied to machine sorting, memory research and social labelling, each adding a new object but not a new root.
items.cn: 这个动词后来被用于机器分类、记忆研究与社会标签，各义只添了新宾语，词根并未改变。

items.en: Source uncertain (exact first citation): the year in which the verb first appears in print is not firmly fixed, and earlier manuscript uses may exist that are not recorded in standard dictionaries.
items.cn: 来源不确定（确切首见书证）：该动词首次印行的年份没有定论，可能存在标准词典未收录的更早手稿用例。

note.en: Group one holds family members that differ in part of speech; group two holds other verbs for arranging things.
note.cn: 第一组是同族中词性不同的词；第二组是其他表示整理安排的动词。

entries.definition: The class itself; the verb needs an object, while the noun is the box the object goes into.
entries.definitionCN: 类别本身；动词需要宾语，而名词是宾语要进的盒子。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning unconditional, not the act of classifying; a categorical answer is a flat one.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，意为无条件的，并非分类动作；断然的答复就是毫不含糊的答复。

entries.definition: A standard for judging, from Greek krinein, to separate or decide; it is not built on the category root.
entries.definitionCN: 判断标准，来自希腊语 krinein「分开、判定」；并非建立在 category 的词根上。

entries.definition: A list or register of items, from a different Greek compound; cataloging records items, categorizing groups them.
entries.definitionCN: 物品清单或登记册，来自另一个希腊复合词；编目是登记项目，归类是分组。

entries.definition: To arrange in classes; it is close to categorize but more common in official and scientific settings.
entries.definitionCN: 安排进类别；与 categorize 相近，但更常用于官方与科学场合。

entries.definition: To arrange by some order; sorting may only sequence items, while categorizing creates groups.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种顺序排列；排序可能只是定次序，而归类会形成组别。

entries.definition: To attach a name to something; labelling is the visible sign of categorizing, not the grouping itself.
entries.definitionCN: 给某物贴上名称；贴标签是归类的可见标志，而非分组本身。

entries.definition: To bring items together; it need not imply that the group has a fixed name or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 把项目聚到一起；不一定意味着这一组有固定名称或规则。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the noun behind the verb, the suffix that makes it act, and the shelves it fills.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：动词背后的名词、使它成为动作的后缀，以及它填满的架子。

normal.en: The noun is category; the verb adds the suffix that means to make or place.
normal.cn: 名词是 category；动词加上表示「使成为、放置」的后缀。

normal.en: The family runs category, categorize, categorization, categorical and categorically.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 category、categorize、categorization、categorical 与 categorically。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the objects it takes: categorize documents, categorize expenses, categorize responses.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示它能带哪些宾语：把文件分类、把支出分项、把答复归类。

normal.en: The pattern with as is a judgement: to categorize a film as a comedy is to declare its kind.
normal.cn: 与表示「作为」的词连用是一种判断：把电影归为喜剧，就是宣布它的种类。

normal.en: Machine learning uses the same verb for filters that sort mail without a person.
normal.cn: 机器学习用同一个动词来指无人参与的邮件分拣过滤器。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing one card into a drawer and closing it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把一张卡片推进抽屉，然后关上。

abstract.en: Picture a shelf where every book faces the same way because its subject decided the place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个书架，每本书都朝同一方向，因为学科决定了位置。

abstract.en: Picture a filter that lets only one colour of sand through each hole.
abstract.cn: 想象一个筛子，每个孔只放行一种颜色的沙。

examples.en: The software can categorize thousands of images in an hour.
examples.cn: 这个软件一小时内能归类数千张图片。

examples.en: Do not categorize a whole neighbourhood by one incident.
examples.cn: 不要因一起事件就给整个街区定性。

examples.en: She categorized the letters by sender before answering any of them.
examples.cn: 她在回信之前先按寄件人把信件归类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 先有「类别」这个盒子，再把东西一件件放进去 → 归类

root: 希腊 katēgoria「公开陈述、谓语」经拉丁 categoria、法语 catégorie 入英语为 category；category 加动词后缀 -ize 成 categorize。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand: an item is sent to the box that matches its features, whether the hand is a clerk's, a mind's, a machine's or a taxonomist's.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一只手展开：某一项被送进与它特征相符的盒子，无论这只手属于职员、心智、机器还是分类学家。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a card sliding into a drawer whose label was decided before the card arrived.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张卡片滑进抽屉，抽屉上的标签在卡片到来之前就已写好。

branches.en: ONE ITEM: the verb starts with a single thing looking for its shelf.
branches.cn: 单项：动词从一件寻找自己架子的东西开始。

branches.en: THE WHOLE SET: repeated placing turns a heap into an order that can be searched later.
branches.cn: 整批：反复放置把一堆东西变成日后可查的次序。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: saying what kind something is can be a verdict, not a harmless move.
branches.cn: 判断：宣布某物属于哪一类，可能是一项裁决，而非无害的搬动。

branches.en: WITHOUT A HAND: rules and neurons perform the same match at different speeds.
branches.cn: 无需人手：规则与神经元以不同速度完成同样的匹配。

branches.en: TWO BOXES: one must answer to ancestry, the other can flatten a person.
branches.cn: 两种盒子：一种必须对亲缘关系负责，另一种可能压平一个人。

intro.en: Categorize is a noun turned into a verb by a suffix, and the whole family can be read from its Greek base.
intro.cn: categorize 是由名词加后缀变成的动词，整个词族都可以从它的希腊语基础读起。

latinIntro.en: Latin categoria carries the Greek noun; English suffixes then build the verb, the action noun and the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 categoria 承载这个希腊名词；英语后缀随后造出动词、动作名词与形容词。

items.example: They categorize the samples by size.
items.exampleCN: 他们按大小把样本归类。

items.meaning: the act or result of classifying

items.exampleCN: 这个分类程序从不休息。
编辑重新归类了这些笔记。

derivatives.meaning: having been placed in a class

definition_zh: 触角；天线；敏锐的感知力
definition_en: a feeler on an insect's head, a device that sends or receives radio waves, or a natural sensitivity to signals
core_image: 头顶伸出的一对细长探杆，向四面试探
scene: 雨后墙角的蚂蚁排成纵队，前面的用头顶细须互相碰触传递方向。 The ants touch antennae to follow the scent trail.
sceneCN: 这里 antenna 是「触角」（第 1 个义项：昆虫头部的感觉器官）；句意为蚂蚁用触角相碰来跟随气味路径。

pos.zh: 触角；天线；感知力

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「触角的」
由本词加指小后缀构成，义为「小触角」

senses.title: An insect's feeler
senses.definition: one of a pair of slender feelers on an insect's head, used for touch and smell
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫头部一对细长的感觉器，用于触觉与嗅觉
senses.example: The beetle waved its antennae to test the air.
senses.exampleCN: 甲虫摆动触角试探空气。
senses.why: Latin antenna first meant the yard of a sail; its long projecting shape was borrowed by naturalists for the insect's feelers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 antenna 原指帆船上的横桁；其细长外伸的形状被博物学家借用来指昆虫的触角。

senses.title: A radio or television aerial
senses.definition: a metal device that sends out or picks up radio waves
senses.definitionCN: 发送或接收无线电波的金属装置
senses.example: The old radio needs a longer antenna to pick up that station.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧收音机需要更长的天线才能收到那个电台。
senses.why: Wireless engineers reused the same word for the projecting rods on a roof, because a mast-yard and an aerial share the long arm reaching into the air.
senses.whyCN: 无线电工程师把同一个词用给屋顶上外伸的金属杆，因为帆桁与天线都是伸向空中的长臂。

senses.title: A sensitivity to signals
senses.definition: a natural ability to notice signs or opportunities
senses.definitionCN: 察觉迹象或机会的天赋
senses.example: A good reporter has an antenna for a story others miss.
senses.exampleCN: 好记者对别人漏掉的新闻有敏锐的嗅觉。
senses.why: If feelers detect what is faintly there, the word can name a person's inner feeler for trends and moods.
senses.whyCN: 既然触角能察觉微弱存在，这个词便可指名一个人对趋势与情绪的内在触角。

intro.en: Antenna began as the name of a sail yard, was borrowed for insect feelers, and was borrowed again for wireless aerials.
intro.cn: antenna 最初指帆船横桁，先被借去指昆虫触角，又被借去指无线电天线。

items.en: antenna was the yard of a ship's sail, a long spar reaching across the mast.
items.cn: antenna 指帆船上的横桁，是一根横过桅杆的长杆。

items.en: The Roman writer Pliny used antenna for the feelers of insects.
items.cn: 罗马作家普林尼用 antenna 指昆虫的触角。

items.en: Naturalists kept the insect sense alive in scientific descriptions.
items.cn: 博物学家在科学描述中保留了昆虫触角义。

items.en: English took antenna first as a term of natural history.
items.cn: 英语先把这个词用作博物学术语。

items.en: With radio, the old word was extended to the rods that send and catch waves.
items.cn: 随着无线电出现，这个旧词被扩展到发送与接收电波的金属杆。

items.en: Modern English uses the plural antennae for insects and antennas for aerials.
items.cn: 现代英语中昆虫多用复数 antennae，天线多用 antennas。

note.en: The first group gathers words that are close in spelling but unrelated in meaning; the second gathers words for feelers and wave receivers.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写相近但意义无关的词；第二组收表示触角与电波接收装置的词。

entries.definition: A song of praise or a national song.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「颂歌、国歌」。

entries.definition: A branched horn of a deer.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「鹿角」。

entries.definition: The insect plural, kept from Latin for feelers.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，昆虫触角的复数，沿用拉丁形式。

entries.definition: A British word for the device that picks up radio or television signals.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，英式用法，义为「天线」，接收无线电或电视信号。

entries.definition: A general word for an animal's organ of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「触须」，泛指动物的触觉器官。

entries.definition: A tall pole that holds an aerial or a sail.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「桅杆、天线杆」，支撑天线或帆的高杆。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the two plurals and the common aerial phrases; the abstract hooks picture a long feeler probing the air.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用两个复数形式与常见天线搭配；抽象记忆点想象一根细长触须在空中试探。

normal.en: Antennae is the insect plural, antennas the aerial plural.
normal.cn: antennae 是昆虫触角的复数，antennas 是天线的复数。

normal.en: A radio antenna catches waves; a satellite antenna faces the sky.
normal.cn: radio antenna 接收电波；satellite antenna 朝向天空。

normal.en: Latin antenna meant a sail yard before it meant a feeler.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 先指帆桁，后才指触角。

normal.en: The adjective is antennal, used in biology for feeler structures.
normal.cn: 形容词是 antennal，生物学中表示「触角的」。

normal.en: A good antenna for news is the figurative pattern worth remembering.
normal.cn: a good antenna for news 是值得记住的比喻用法。

abstract.en: Picture two thin whips tapping the air ahead of an ant.
abstract.cn: 想象两根细鞭在蚂蚁前方轻触空气。

abstract.en: Picture a long metal rod on a roof pointing at the horizon.
abstract.cn: 想象屋顶上一根长金属杆指向地平线。

abstract.en: Picture a listener who senses a rumor before anyone says it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个在别人开口前就嗅到传闻的听众。

examples.en: The moth's antennae detect the scent of a mate.
examples.cn: 飞蛾的触角能察觉配偶的气味。

examples.en: He climbed the roof to fix the television antenna.
examples.cn: 他爬上屋顶修理电视天线。

examples.en: She has an antenna for what the market will want next.
examples.cn: 她对市场下一步的需求有敏锐的嗅觉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安泰娜」——头顶伸出两根细长探杆，在空气里四处试探，这就是触角。

root: 拉丁语 antenna（帆船横桁）→ 昆虫触角 → 无线电天线；核心义是「向外伸出、探测空中的细长装置」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the insect feeler, to the wireless aerial, to the figurative inner feeler for signals.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从昆虫触角，走到无线电天线，再到比喻性的内在感知力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long feeler reaching out and probing the air
core.cn: 核心意象：一根向外伸出并试探空气的长触须

branches.en: The insect's paired feelers for touch and scent.
branches.cn: 昆虫用于触觉与嗅觉的一对触角。

branches.en: The roof rod that sends and receives waves.
branches.cn: 屋顶上发送与接收电波的金属杆。

branches.en: A person's figurative feeler for trends and moods.
branches.cn: 一个人对趋势与情绪的比喻性触角。

branches.en: Both senses share the long outward-reaching shape.
branches.cn: 两个义项共享细长外伸的形状。

branches.en: Detection links the aerial and the inner sensor.
branches.cn: 「探测」把天线与内在感知连在一起。

intro.en: The word carries Latin antenna unchanged, and its family uses the adjective and diminutive endings -al and -ule.
intro.cn: 这个词原样保留拉丁语 antenna，其词族使用形容词与指小后缀 -al 与 -ule。

latinIntro.en: Latin antenna is the direct source, so the Latin entries record the sail-yard noun and the derived adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 antenna 是直接来源，因此拉丁条目记录「帆桁」名词与派生形容词。

definition_zh: 平衡；均衡；（物理）平衡态；（经济）市场均衡；（情绪）平静
definition_en: a state in which opposing forces or influences are balanced, so nothing tends to change
core_image: 一架天平两端重量相等，指针停在中央刻度上
scene: 走钢丝的人在风中调整手里的长杆，让身体停在正中不再倾斜。 The tightrope walker adjusted the pole until the body reached equilibrium above the wire.
sceneCN: 走钢丝的人在风中调整长杆，让身体停在正中不再倾斜；句中的 equilibrium 指「相反的力量相抵、系统不再偏移的状态」（第 1 个义项：物理意义上的受力平衡）。图中可辨识物件：钢丝、长杆、稳定姿态、远处的风旗。

pos.zh: 平衡；均衡；平静（复数 equilibria）
均衡的（作定语，如 equilibrium state）

senses.title: Balance of physical forces
senses.definition: the state in which the forces acting on a body cancel out
senses.definitionCN: 作用在一个物体上的力相互抵消的状态
senses.example: The tightrope walker adjusted the pole until the body reached equilibrium above the wire.
senses.exampleCN: 走钢丝的人调整长杆，直到身体在钢丝上方达到平衡。
senses.why: The Latin word joins 'level' and 'scales', so the first sense is simply a pair of pans that no longer tips.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词把「平」与「天平」合在一起，因此第一义就是一架不再倾斜的天平。

senses.title: Chemical balance of two reactions
senses.definition: the state in which a forward reaction and its reverse proceed at equal rates
senses.definitionCN: 正反应与逆反应速率相等的状态
senses.example: The mixture reaches equilibrium when both reactions run at the same rate.
senses.exampleCN: 当两个反应以相同速率进行时，混合物达到平衡。
senses.why: Two opposing processes cancelling is the same picture as two weights cancelling, applied to rates instead of forces.
senses.whyCN: 两个相反过程相互抵消，与两个重量相抵是同一幅图，只是把力换成了速率。

senses.title: Market balance of supply and demand
senses.definition: the price and quantity at which the amount offered equals the amount wanted
senses.definitionCN: 供给量与需求量相等时的价格与数量
senses.example: The market found equilibrium at a price neither side had expected.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在一个双方都没预料到的价位上达到均衡。
senses.why: Economics borrowed the word because a market that stops moving looks like a beam that has levelled.
senses.whyCN: 经济学借用这个词，因为停止波动的市场就像一根已经放平的横梁。

senses.title: Emotional composure
senses.definition: a calm inner state in which opposing feelings do not pull a person about
senses.definitionCN: 相反情绪不再把人拉来拉去的平静内心状态
senses.example: Years of practice gave her an equilibrium that no insult could shake.
senses.exampleCN: 多年历练给了她一种任何侮辱都撼不动的平静。
senses.why: The metaphor moves inward: the opposing weights become feelings, and the level beam becomes a steady temper.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内心：相抵的重量变成情绪，水平的横梁变成稳定的性情。

senses.title: Biological and ecological balance
senses.definition: the steady internal or ecological state that a living system maintains
senses.definitionCN: 生命系统维持的内部或生态稳定状态
senses.example: Reef fish keep a rough equilibrium with the corals they feed on.
senses.exampleCN: 礁鱼与它们取食的珊瑚之间维持着大致平衡。
senses.why: A living system held steady by opposing processes is the same idea as a body held steady by opposing forces.
senses.whyCN: 生命系统靠相反过程维持稳定，与物体靠相反的力维持稳定是同一想法。

senses.title: A steady state with no tendency to change
senses.titleCN: 不再有变化趋势的稳定状态
senses.definition: a general condition in which nothing pushes the system away from where it is
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何因素把系统推离原位的总体状态
senses.example: After the shock, the system slowly returned to equilibrium.
senses.exampleCN: 冲击过后，系统慢慢回到平衡。
senses.why: Stripped of physics and markets, the core is simply rest, a state that no push disturbs.
senses.whyCN: 去掉物理与市场的具体内容，核心就是静止——一种没有推力能打扰的状态。

senses.title: A strategy nobody gains by changing
senses.titleCN: 无人因单独改变而获益的策略均衡
senses.definition: in game theory, a profile of choices in which no player gains by switching alone
senses.definitionCN: 博弈论中任何一方单独改变选择都无利可图的局面
senses.example: Neither firm could improve its payoff, so the pair settled into equilibrium.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司都无法提高收益，于是这一对选择进入均衡。
senses.why: The word is used for a balance of incentives rather than of forces, yet the shape is the same.
senses.whyCN: 这里平衡的是激励而非力，但形状仍然相同。

senses.title: Thermal equilibrium
senses.definition: the condition in which two bodies in contact exchange no net heat
senses.definitionCN: 两个接触物体之间没有净热量交换的状态
senses.example: The two blocks reached thermal equilibrium at the same temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 两块物体在同一温度下达到热平衡。
senses.why: Heat flow stops exactly when the two sides level off, which is the scales image made literal.
senses.whyCN: 热流恰在两侧齐平之时停止，这正是天平意象的字面版本。

intro.en: Equilibrium is Latin aequilibrium 'level balance', from aequus 'level, equal' and libra 'balance, scales'. English took it in the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: equilibrium 来自拉丁 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」，由 aequus「平的、相等的」与 libra「天平」构成，十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal' and also 'calm, fair'. It gives equal, equity, equator and equable.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、齐的、相等的」，也表示「平静、公正」；它衍生 equal、equity、equator 与 equable。

items.en: Libra meant 'balance, scales' and also a unit of weight, roughly a pound; the zodiac sign took the same name.
items.cn: libra 意为「天平、秤」，也指一种重量单位，约合一磅；黄道十二宫的「天秤座」沿用此名。

items.en: Aequus plus libra produced aequilibrium, 'a level balance', used for physical balance and later for balance of mind.
items.cn: aequus 加 libra 构成 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」，先用于物理平衡，后也用于心境。

items.en: English adopted the word in the 1600s, at first for physical and mechanical balance.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪吸收这个词，最初用于物理与力学的平衡。

items.en: Nineteenth-century economics applied it to the price at which supply and demand meet, and the term became central to the discipline.
items.cn: 十九世纪经济学把它用于供需相遇的价格，这个词随后成为该学科的核心术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: whether English took the word directly from Latin or through French equilibre is not settled, and the earliest citation date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语是直接从拉丁语借入，还是经法语 equilibre 传入，尚无定论；最早书证年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin stock that are easily confused; group two holds near terms for balance.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源、容易混淆的词；第二组是表示平衡的近义词。

entries.definition: Built on aequus alone: a steady, unvarying temper or climate, with no second element meaning balance.
entries.definitionCN: 只由 aequus 构成：指平稳不变的性情或气候，并没有表示「天平」的第二部分。

entries.definition: From aequus plus animus 'mind': calmness of mind, a cousin in meaning but not built on the scales image.
entries.definitionCN: 由 aequus 加 animus「心」构成：心平气和，意思相近，但并不建立在天平意象上。

entries.definition: From aequitas, 'evenness, fairness': justice or ownership value, not a physical balance.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aequitas「均平、公正」：指公平或产权价值，不是物理平衡。

entries.definition: An English formation from equi- 'equal' and poise 'weight': a balanced state, close in meaning but not from the Latin noun.
entries.definitionCN: 英语自造词，由 equi-「相等」与 poise「重量」构成：平衡状态，意思接近但并非来自那个拉丁名词。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for an even distribution of weight or power; it is the everyday counterpart of equilibrium.
entries.definitionCN: 表示重量或力量均匀分布的日常词，是 equilibrium 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: The tendency to stay in place when pushed; equilibrium is the state, stability is how well it holds.
entries.definitionCN: 受推时保持原位的倾向；equilibrium 是状态，stability 是这种状态有多稳。

entries.definition: The specific biological term for a body holding its internal conditions steady; equilibrium is the wider word.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体维持内部条件稳定的专门术语；equilibrium 范围更广。

entries.definition: A state of standstill, often used of fluids or history; it names stillness rather than balanced forces.
entries.definitionCN: 停滞状态，常用于流体或历史；指静止而非力量相抵。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two Latin pieces, the fixed phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个拉丁成分、固定搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: Aequus 'level' plus libra 'scales': a pair of pans that stops tipping.
normal.cn: aequus「平」加 libra「天平」：一对不再倾斜的秤盘。

normal.en: The family runs equilibrium, equilibrate, equilibration, disequilibrium and nonequilibrium.
normal.cn: 同族词有 equilibrium、equilibrate、equilibration、disequilibrium 与 nonequilibrium。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: in equilibrium, thermal equilibrium, market equilibrium, stable equilibrium.
normal.cn: 固定说法：处于平衡、热平衡、市场均衡、稳定平衡。

normal.en: The same first element appears in equal, equity, equator and equable.
normal.cn: 同一前半出现在 equal、equity、equator 与 equable 中。

normal.en: Aequus also meant calm, which is why the word can describe a steady temper.
normal.cn: aequus 也含「平静」之意，所以这个词能形容稳定的性情。

abstract.en: Picture a beam that stops moving the moment its two pans carry the same weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根横梁，两端负重相等的那一刻就停止摆动。

abstract.en: Picture a room where heat stops crossing the wall because both sides are equally warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，两侧一样暖时热量就不再穿墙。

abstract.en: Picture a mind pulled from both sides until the pull cancels and it simply stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心被两侧拉扯，直到拉力相抵，它就原地不动。

examples.en: The reaction mixture took twenty minutes to reach equilibrium.
examples.cn: 反应混合物用了二十分钟达到平衡。

examples.en: Higher tariffs pushed the market away from its old equilibrium.
examples.cn: 更高的关税把市场推离了原来的均衡。

examples.en: She listened to the whole complaint with an unshaken equilibrium.
examples.cn: 她以毫不动摇的平静听完了整段抱怨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equi（相等）+ librium（天平）——两边相等，秤就平了」

root: 拉丁 aequilibrium「水平的平衡」= aequus「平的、相等的」+ libra「天平、秤」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image, a beam that levels: forces, reaction rates, market price, temper, living systems, plain rest, incentives and heat flow.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项围绕同一幅图——一根放平的横梁：力、反应速率、市场价格、性情、生命系统、单纯的静止、激励与热流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scales whose pointer rests exactly at the middle mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：一架指针正停在中央刻度的天平。

branches.en: WEIGHT: mechanical forces and heat flow both stop when the two sides level.
branches.cn: 重量：力学上的力与热流，都在两侧齐平时停止。

branches.en: NATURAL PROCESSES: reaction rates match, and living systems hold their inner conditions steady.
branches.cn: 自然过程：反应速率相符，生命系统则维持内部条件稳定。

branches.en: SETTLED MARKET AND MERE REST: price stops moving, and any system stops being pushed.
branches.cn: 市场与静止：价格不再变动，任何系统也不再被推动。

branches.en: MIND: composure is a balance of feelings that nobody can see.
branches.cn: 内心：平静是一种看不见的情绪平衡。

branches.en: INCENTIVES: no player gains by moving alone, so the choices stay put.
branches.cn: 激励：无人因单独改变而获益，选择因此停在原处。

intro.en: Equilibrium is two Latin words welded together, and each half still builds English words on its own.
intro.cn: equilibrium 由两个拉丁词焊接而成，两半各自仍能构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus gives equal, equity, equator and equable; libra gives Libra and the sense of weighing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus 衍生 equal、equity、equator 与 equable；libra 衍生 Libra 及「称量」之义。

items.example: The first half of the word carries the idea of evenness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词的前半带着「均平」的意思。

items.meaning: balance, scales; a unit of weight
items.example: The second half supplies the picture of weighing.

items.exampleCN: 两个腔室一夜之间达到平衡。

items.example: The shock caused a brief disequilibrium.
items.exampleCN: 冲击造成了短暂的失衡。
非平衡系统需要持续供能。

items.example: He kept an equable temper all day.
Pay equity was the central demand.

latinEntries.structure: aequus, aequa, aequum (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 共振；共鸣；洪亮的回响；物理学中系统在特定频率下的强响应
definition_en: a strong sympathetic vibration produced when a system is driven at its natural frequency, or the deep echoing quality of a sound
core_image: 一个长音正好撞上玻璃杯的固有节律，杯壁越摆越大，直到裂开
scene: 歌剧演员唱出一个长音，玻璃杯突然裂开。 The glass shattered because the note matched its resonance exactly.
sceneCN: 这里 resonance 指「系统在固有频率下产生的强响应」（第 1 个义项：外驱频率与固有频率相合时的剧烈振动）；句意：玻璃杯碎裂，是因为那个音正好与它的共振频率相合。图中可辨识物件：玻璃杯、歌者、声波环、碎裂纹。

pos.zh: 共振；共鸣；回响（可数或不可数）

senses.title: Driven vibration at a natural frequency
senses.titleCN: 在固有频率下被驱动的强振动
senses.definition: the large vibration that occurs when a system is pushed at the rate it naturally prefers
senses.definitionCN: 当系统被以它天然偏好的速率推动时出现的剧烈振动
senses.example: The bridge collapsed when wind matched its resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 风与桥的共振相合时，桥塌了。
senses.why: Latin resonare means 'to sound again', and a system driven at its own rate answers every push with a larger one, so the name records the answering.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语意为「再次发声」，而被以自身速率驱动的系统会对每一次推动给出更大的回应，名字记下的正是这种回应。

senses.title: A deep, full sound
senses.definition: the rich, prolonged quality of a sound that seems to fill a space
senses.definitionCN: 一种似乎填满空间的丰厚而持久的声音品质
senses.example: The cello's low strings have a warm resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 大提琴的低音弦有温暖的共鸣。
senses.why: A body that answers many frequencies at once sounds full, so the physical response became a word for tonal richness.
senses.whyCN: 能同时应和许多频率的物体听起来饱满，因此物理响应成了音色丰厚的说法。

senses.title: Magnetic resonance imaging
senses.definition: the technique in which atomic nuclei in a magnetic field absorb and re-emit radio waves at characteristic frequencies
senses.definitionCN: 原子核在磁场中于特征频率吸收并再发射无线电波的技术
senses.example: The scan uses magnetic resonance to map soft tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 这项扫描利用磁共振来成像软组织。
senses.why: Nuclei are tiny magnets with fixed precession rates, and flipping them at exactly that rate is resonance in the strict physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 原子核是带固定进动速率的小磁体，恰好在那个速率上把它翻转，就是严格物理意义上的共振。

senses.title: Resonance in chemical bonding
senses.definition: the description of a molecule as a weighted blend of several possible electron arrangements
senses.definitionCN: 把分子描述为几种可能电子排布的加权混合
senses.example: Benzene is drawn as resonance between two ring structures.
senses.exampleCN: 苯被画成两种环状结构之间的共振。
senses.why: Chemists borrowed the word because the true electron pattern behaves like a system answering several forms at once.
senses.whyCN: 化学家借这个词，是因为真实的电子分布像同时应和几种形式的系统。

senses.title: Emotional or cultural echo
senses.definition: the quality of an idea, story or image that stirs a strong shared response in an audience
senses.definitionCN: 一个想法、故事或形象在受众中激起强烈共同回应的品质
senses.example: The film found resonance with readers who had also left home.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片在同样离家的读者中引起了共鸣。
senses.why: Sympathetic vibration is a ready metaphor for a feeling that is set off in one person by something in another.
senses.whyCN: 应和振动天然适合比喻一种由他人之物在自身激起的感受。

senses.title: Regular gravitational timing
senses.definition: a situation in which orbiting bodies repeatedly pull on one another in a fixed rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 轨道上的天体以固定节律反复相互牵引的情形
senses.example: The moons are locked in orbital resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 这些卫星被锁在轨道共振之中。
senses.why: The repeated gravitational pushes arrive at the same phase of each orbit, which is the astronomical version of driving a system at its own rate.
senses.whyCN: 反复的引力推动落在每次轨道的同一相位上，这正是「以自身速率驱动系统」的天文版本。

senses.title: A short-lived particle state
senses.definition: a very brief particle state that appears as a peak in a scattering experiment
senses.definitionCN: 在散射实验里表现为峰值的极短暂粒子状态
senses.example: The team reported a new resonance in the collision data.
senses.exampleCN: 团队在碰撞数据中报告了一个新的共振态。
senses.why: A particle that lives too briefly to be seen leaves a peak at one energy, the same signature as a driven oscillator.
senses.whyCN: 寿命短到看不见的粒子会在某一能量处留下峰值，其印记与受驱振子相同。

senses.title: Tuned response in a circuit
senses.definition: the condition in which an electrical circuit responds most strongly at one chosen frequency
senses.definitionCN: 电路在某一选定频率上响应最强的状态
senses.example: The radio circuit reaches resonance at the station's frequency.
senses.exampleCN: 收音机电路在电台频率上达到共振。
senses.why: Capacitance and inductance exchange energy in a rhythm, and matching an incoming signal to that rhythm is electrical resonance.
senses.whyCN: 电容与电感按节律交换能量，把来信号与这一节律相合，就是电学共振。

intro.en: Resonance comes from Latin resonantia 'echo', from resonare 'to sound again', built on re- 'again' and sonare 'to sound'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: resonance 来自拉丁 resonantia「回声」，而它出自 resonare「再次发声」，由「再次」与「发声」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sonus meant 'sound, tone'. Its deeper origin is not established; the usual link to a root meaning 'to sound' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: sonus 意为「声音、音调」。其更早来源没有定论；把它与表示「发声」的词根联系起来的说法属于重构。

items.en: Resonare meant 'to resound, to return a sound', as a hall or a cave returns a shout.
items.cn: resonare 意为「回响、把声音送回来」，如厅堂或洞穴把喊声送回。

items.en: The noun resonantia named an echo or a re-echoing, the abstract result of that returning sound.
items.cn: 名词 resonantia 指回声或反复回响，是那种返回之声的抽象结果。

items.en: English borrowed resonance in the sixteenth century for an echoing sound, and it remained chiefly a word about acoustics.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 resonance，指回响的声音，长期主要是声学词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century physics applied it to any system driven at its natural rate, and chemistry, astronomy and medicine each took a share.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，物理学把它用于任何被自身速率驱动的系统，化学、天文学与医学各取一支。

items.en: First dates for the technical senses are approximate; the Latin chain is fully recorded.
items.cn: 各技术义的最早年代为约数；拉丁语链条有完整记录。

note.en: Group one holds same-root words and one dangerous look-alike from a different root; group two holds near sound and vibration words.
note.cn: 第一组是同根词与一个来自不同词根的易混形近词；第二组是邻近的声音与振动词。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something that resounds or is driven at its natural rate; it is not a separate physical effect.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物回响或在其固有速率上被驱动的形容词；它不是另一种物理效应。

entries.definition: From Latin residere 'to remain sitting', built on sedere 'to sit': a place where one lives, with no sound involved.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁语「留在坐着」，构于「坐」：指居住之所，与声音无关。

entries.definition: Latin con- 'together' plus sonare: sounds that agree when played together, a musical judgement rather than a driven vibration.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「共同」加「发声」：合奏时相合的声音，是音乐判断而非受驱振动。

entries.definition: Latin dis- 'apart' plus sonare: sounds that clash, the opposite judgement to consonance and unrelated to resonance.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁「分开」加「发声」：相冲的声音，与「协和」相反，也与共振无关。

entries.definition: A sound reflected back once from a surface; resonance is a sustained response, not a single bounce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音从一个表面反射回来一次；而这个词指持续响应，不是一次反弹。

entries.definition: The prolonging of sound by repeated reflections in a room; it is the acoustic result that resonance can help produce.
entries.definitionCN: 声音在室内经多次反射而延长；它是共振可能促成的声学结果。

entries.definition: Any rapid back-and-forth movement; resonance is the special case where the movement grows because it is driven at the right rate.
entries.definitionCN: 任何快速的往复运动；这个词是其特例，因被以正确速率驱动而增大。

entries.definition: A feeling shared with another person; the word was once used for physical sympathetic vibration and now mostly means emotional agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 与他人共享的感受；这个词曾用于物理上的应和振动，如今多指情感上的相合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin re- 'again' plus sonare 'to sound': a sound that answers again and again.
normal.cn: 拉丁「再次」加「发声」：一再应答的声音。

normal.en: The family runs resonance, resonant, resonate, resonator, resonantly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括共振、洪亮的、共鸣、共鸣器、以共鸣的方式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: magnetic resonance, resonance frequency, emotional resonance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：磁共振、共振频率、情感共鸣。

normal.en: The same sound-root appears in consonant and dissonant, both judgements of harmony.
normal.cn: 同一「发声」词根出现在协和与不协和里，两者都是对和声的判断。

normal.en: Beware residence: it comes from sitting, not sounding, and only looks alike.
normal.cn: 当心那个表示「居住」的形近词：它出自「坐」而非「发声」，只是长得像。

abstract.en: Picture a swing pushed at exactly the moment it comes back, so each push adds height.
abstract.cn: 想象秋千荡回的那一刻恰好被推一下，于是每一推都增加高度。

abstract.en: Picture a room that repeats a single note until the note seems to own the space.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间反复送回同一个音，直到那个音仿佛占有了空间。

abstract.en: Picture two tuning forks of the same pitch, one waking the other without being touched.
abstract.cn: 想象两支同音高的音叉，一支未被触碰却唤醒了另一支。

examples.en: The singer broke the glass by finding its resonance.
examples.cn: 歌手找到玻璃的共振点，把它唱碎了。

examples.en: The poem has a resonance that outlasts its century.
examples.cn: 这首诗有一种超越它那个时代的共鸣。

examples.en: The circuit is tuned to resonance at one frequency only.
examples.cn: 这个电路只在一个频率上被调到共振。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ son（声）+ ance」——声音一再回来，就是共鸣

root: 拉丁 resonantia「回声」← resonare「再次发声」= re-「再次」+ sonare「发声」；sonus「声音」更早来源不确定。英语 resonance。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one pattern of answering: a driven system, a full tone, a medical scan, a chemical blend, an emotional echo, an orbital rhythm, a particle peak and a tuned circuit.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个「应答」模式：受驱系统、饱满音色、医学扫描、化学混合、情感回声、轨道节律、粒子峰值与调谐电路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note that matches a glass's own rhythm, so every push arrives at the right moment and the swing grows.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个与玻璃固有节律相合的音，每次推动都恰好落在对的时刻，摆幅便越来越大。

branches.en: THE DRIVEN SYSTEM: a glass and a radio circuit both grow loud when pushed at their own rate.
branches.cn: 受驱系统：玻璃杯与收音机电路在被以自身速率推动时都会变得强烈。

branches.en: THE FULL VOICE: a body answering many rates at once sounds rich and prolonged.
branches.cn: 饱满的声音：同时应和许多速率的物体听起来丰厚而持久。

branches.en: THE MEASURED PEAK: nuclei and short-lived particles both mark resonance as a sharp maximum in a scan.
branches.cn: 被测的峰：原子核与短命粒子都把共振表现为扫描图上的尖峰。

branches.en: THE BLEND: chemistry uses the word for a molecule that answers several electron arrangements at once.
branches.cn: 混合：化学用这个词指同时应和几种电子排布的分子。

branches.en: THE RHYTHM ELSEWHERE: a story stirs a shared feeling, and moons pull one another in step.
branches.cn: 别处的节律：故事激起共同感受，卫星则同步相互牵引。

intro.en: Resonance is a Latin abstract noun built from a prefix, a verb of sounding and a noun ending, all three of which recur in English.
intro.cn: resonance 是拉丁抽象名词，由前缀、发声动词与名词结尾构成，三者在英语里都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sonare and sonus also give consonant, dissonant, sonata and sonar's namesake; re- adds the idea of return.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sonare 与 sonus 还衍生出 consonant、dissonant、sonata 以及 sonar 的同源成分；re- 增添「返回」之意。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement that comes back.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出折返的运动。

items.example: The verb covers any sounding, sung or struck.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词涵盖任何发声，唱或敲皆可。

items.example: The noun names the thing that returns.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被送回来的那个东西。

items.example: The hall resounded with the choir.
The noun names the state of answering sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指声音应答的状态。

items.example: The note found the glass's resonance.
items.exampleCN: 那个音找到了玻璃的共振点。

items.example: A resonant voice fills the hall.

items.meaning: to echo; to strike a shared feeling
items.example: The story resonated with the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这个故事在听众中引起共鸣。

latinEntries.structure: sonare, sono, sonavi, sonatum (v., first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to sound, to make a noise

definition_zh: 恶化；加剧；激怒
definition_en: the act of making a bad condition, problem, or feeling worse or more intense
core_image: 一滴苦汁搅进清水，越搅越苦、越难下咽
scene: 医生翻看病历，发现病人昨夜喘得比前一天更厉害。 The nurse noted an exacerbation of asthma after the cold snap.
sceneCN: 这里 exacerbation 是「加重、恶化」（第 1 个义项：病情突然加重）；句意：护士注意到寒潮过后病人的哮喘加重了。

pos.zh: 恶化；加剧；激怒

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀 -ation 还原的动词，义为「使恶化；加剧；激怒」
动词加 -ing 构成的形容词，义为「使情况恶化的；令人恼火的」
过去分词转作的形容词，义为「被加重的；被激怒的」

senses.title: A worsening of a disease
senses.definition: a sudden increase in the severity of a disease or of its symptoms
senses.definitionCN: 疾病或其症状严重程度的突然上升
senses.example: The patient was admitted with an acute exacerbation of asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 病人因哮喘急性加重而入院。
senses.why: Latin acerbus means bitter and harsh, and exacerbare means to make a thing more bitter, so the noun first names a disease turning harsher.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 就是把东西弄得更苦，所以这个名词最先指病情转向更凶的那一刻。

senses.title: An increase in the severity of a problem
senses.definition: the act of making a problem, a conflict, or a bad situation worse
senses.definitionCN: 使问题、冲突或糟糕局面变得更严重的行为或过程
senses.example: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。
senses.why: The medical image spread outward: any condition that can be made bitter can be made worse, so the noun came to name the sharpening of social and political troubles.
senses.whyCN: 医学意象向外扩散：凡是可以变「苦」的状况都可以被弄得更糟，于是这个名词也指社会与政治困境的加剧。

senses.title: The act of irritating or provoking
senses.definition: the act of making a person angry or irritated
senses.definitionCN: 使某人生气或恼怒的行为
senses.example: His calm questions were an exacerbation rather than a comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 他平静的追问与其说是安慰，不如说是激怒。
senses.why: The Latin verb also meant to provoke, because bitterness was felt as a sting, and the noun kept that older sense of pricking someone into anger.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词还含「挑动」义，因为苦涩被感受为一种刺；名词保留了更早的「刺人发怒」这一层。

senses.title: A countable flare-up episode
senses.definition: a distinct episode in which symptoms flare up and then settle again
senses.definitionCN: 症状突然发作、随后又平复的一次独立病程
senses.example: She recorded three exacerbations in the past year.
senses.exampleCN: 她记录下去年有三次急性加重。
senses.why: Doctors needed to count these events, so the noun moved from an abstract worsening to a single attack, and the plural marks one episode at a time.
senses.whyCN: 医生需要清点这类事件，名词便从抽象的「恶化」转为一次具体的发作，复数正指一次一次单独的发作。

intro.en: Exacerbation comes from Latin acerbus, bitter or harsh, through the verb exacerbare, to make worse or to provoke.
intro.cn: exacerbation 源自拉丁语 acerbus（苦涩、猛烈），经由动词 exacerbare（使恶化、激怒）而来。

items.en: Acerbus means harsh, bitter, or sour, and its sharper cousin acer means keen or cutting.
items.cn: acerbus 意为猛烈、苦涩、酸；它更尖利的近亲 acer 意为锐利、锋利的。

items.en: The verb exacerbare joins ex- to acerbus and means to make harsh, to aggravate, or to provoke.
items.cn: 动词 exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成，意为使变苦、加重或激怒。

items.en: The action noun exacerbatio names the making worse of a condition or of a temper.
items.cn: 动作名词 exacerbatio 指病情或情绪的加重。

items.en: Medical writing in French carries exacerbation forward as a term for a graver turn of illness.
items.cn: 法语医学文献把 exacerbation 传下去，用作病情转向更重的术语。

items.en: English takes the word as a learned medical noun for the sharpening of a disease.
items.cn: 英语接受了这个词，把它当作表示病情加重的学术医学名词。

items.en: Modern usage widens it to problems, conflicts, and countable attacks of illness.
items.cn: 现代用法把它扩展到问题、冲突，以及可数的病情发作。

note.en: Exacerbation sits in the bitter family of acerbus, beside the verb exacerbate, and near the plain worsening words.
note.cn: exacerbation 属于 acerbus 的「苦涩」词族，与动词 exacerbate 同根，也与平实的「恶化」类词相邻。

entries.definition: to make a bad situation or feeling worse
entries.definitionCN: 使糟糕的局面或情绪变得更糟

entries.definition: bitter or sharp in tone
entries.definitionCN: 言辞尖酸刻薄的；同出「苦涩」词根

entries.definition: a feeling of intense irritation
entries.definitionCN: 极度恼火——与 exacerbation 只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 asper「粗糙」）

entries.definition: the act of making something worse
entries.definitionCN: 加重；使恶化

entries.definition: the process of becoming worse in quality or condition
entries.definitionCN: 质量或状况变坏的过程

entries.definition: a sudden burst of a disease or of anger
entries.definitionCN: 疾病的突然发作；怒气的突然爆发

normalIntro.en: Exacerbation keeps the Latin taste of bitterness: whatever is exacerbated has been made harsher.
normalIntro.cn: exacerbation 保留着拉丁语「苦涩」的味道：被加剧的东西都变得更凶了。

normal.en: Acute exacerbation is a fixed medical phrase for a sudden flare-up.
normal.cn: acute exacerbation 是固定医学说法，指突然的急性加重。

normal.en: Exacerbate is the verb, while exasperate is a different word with a different root.
normal.cn: exacerbate 是动词，exasperate 则是另一个词，词根并不相同。

normal.en: The prefix ex- pushes the meaning outward, so the condition breaks out worse.
normal.cn: 前缀 ex- 把意义向外推，于是病情「爆」得更凶。

normal.en: Planners speak of exacerbating traffic problems, meaning the jams get worse.
normal.cn: 规划者会说「加剧交通问题」，意思就是堵得更厉害。

normal.en: Hospitals count exacerbations, so the plural is common in case reports.
normal.cn: 医院会统计发作次数，所以复数形式在病例报告中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture one bitter drop stirred into clear water until every sip turns harsh.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴苦汁搅进清水，每一口都变得更苦。

abstract.en: Imagine a hairline crack in a dam widening as the water presses on it.
abstract.cn: 想象堤坝上一道细缝在水压下越裂越宽。

abstract.en: Feel a splinter under the skin: the more you touch it, the angrier the spot grows.
abstract.cn: 想象皮肤下扎了一根刺，越碰那处越发红发火。

examples.en: The heat wave brought an exacerbation of her breathing problems.
examples.cn: 热浪使她的呼吸问题加重了。

examples.en: Poverty is both a result and an exacerbation of the crisis.
examples.cn: 贫困既是危机的结果，也是危机的加剧因素。

examples.en: Doctors counted four exacerbations during the winter.
examples.cn: 医生统计出冬季有四次急性加重。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挨个撒盐」——读起来像挨个往伤口撒盐，越撒越疼，就是「恶化、激怒」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 ex-（向外、加强）+ acerbus（苦涩、猛烈）→ 动词 exacerbare（使更苦、激怒）→ 名词 exacerbatio → 英语 exacerbation，核心义「把状况弄得更苦更凶」。

sensesIntro.en: Exacerbation starts as the medical worsening of a disease, widens to any problem made worse, keeps the older sense of provocation, and ends as a countable flare-up.
sensesIntro.cn: exacerbation 先是医学上病情的加重，再扩展到任何问题的恶化，又保留更早的「激怒」义，最后成为可数的一次发作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bitter drop stirred into clear water until it turns harsh.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴苦汁搅进清水，直到整杯变苦。

branches.en: A disease turning worse is the medical core of the word.
branches.cn: 病情转为更重，是这个词的医学核心义。

branches.en: Any bad situation can be made harsher, which is the widened sense.
branches.cn: 任何糟糕局面都能被弄得更凶，这是扩展后的义项。

branches.en: The old sense of pricking someone into anger survives beside it.
branches.cn: 「刺人发怒」的旧义一直与它并存。

branches.en: A countable attack is one concrete turn for the worse.
branches.cn: 可数的一次发作，就是一次具体的恶化。

branches.en: A worsened problem and a provoked person are both things made bitter.
branches.cn: 被加剧的问题与被激怒的人，都是被弄「苦」了的对象。

intro.en: Exacerbation is built from the Latin prefix ex-, the root acerbus, bitter, and the noun suffix -ation.
intro.cn: exacerbation 由拉丁语前缀 ex-、词根 acerbus（苦涩）与名词后缀 -ation 组合而成。

latinIntro.en: Latin acerbus means harsh or bitter, and exacerbare means to make harsh or to provoke.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 acerbus 意为苦涩、猛烈，exacerbare 意为使变苦、激怒。

items.example: The prefix ex- intensifies the bitterness.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 加强了「苦」的程度。

items.example: Acerbus describes a sharp and bitter taste.
items.exampleCN: acerbus 描述尖锐苦涩的味道。

items.example: Acer is the sharper cousin of acerbus.
items.exampleCN: acer 是 acerbus 更尖利的近亲。
exacerbare 由 ex- 与 acerbus 合成。

items.example: Exacerbatio is the Latin action noun.
items.exampleCN: exacerbatio 是拉丁语的动作名词。

items.example: The suffix -ation builds a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Do not confuse it with exasperate.
items.exampleCN: 注意不要把它与 exasperate 混淆。

items.example: Exacerbating factors keep the disease active.
items.exampleCN: 加重因素让疾病持续活动。

items.example: Exasperate comes from asper, rough, not from acerbus.
items.exampleCN: exasperate 来自 asper（粗糙），并非来自 acerbus。

items.example: Acerbic wit shares the bitter root.
items.exampleCN: acerbic 的尖刻共享「苦」这个词根。

definition_zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；轻微的；（数学）平凡的；浅薄的
definition_en: of little importance or value, or so simple that it needs no special effort
core_image: 会议桌一端堆着修改用词的纸条，另一端那份预算缺口表始终没人翻开
scene: 会议开了半小时，大家还在争表格里一个无关紧要的用词，真正的预算缺口没人提。 The committee spent an hour on a trivial wording issue while the budget gap went unmentioned.
sceneCN: 这里指重要性很小、不值得花时间（第 1 个义项：微不足道的）；句意为委员会花一小时争一个无关紧要的用词，预算缺口却无人提及。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、修改用词的纸条、预算缺口表、翻开的文件夹。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；浅薄的
（数学）平凡的；显然的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；微不足道的事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地；平凡地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎；轻描淡写」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪的三门基础学科
由同一拉丁词的中性复数构成，义为「琐事；冷知识」

senses.title: Of little importance
senses.definition: too small or unimportant to affect the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 太小或不重要，影响不到主要问题
senses.example: The delay was trivial compared with the cost of a wrong decision.
senses.exampleCN: 与错误决策的代价相比，这点延误微不足道。
senses.why: The word's history runs from the crossroads to the common, and then to the common that no longer matters.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的历史从「三岔路口」走到「平常」，再走到「平常到不再重要」。

senses.title: An everyday trifle
senses.definition: a small everyday detail hardly worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 不值得关注的小日常细节
senses.example: They argued about whose turn it was to water the plants, a trivial matter in a busy week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争该轮到谁浇花，这在忙碌的一周里只是琐事。
senses.why: A matter is trivial when its size, not its difficulty, is the reason to ignore it.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被称为琐事，是因为它小，而不是因为它难。

senses.title: A cost too small to count
senses.definition: an expense so small that it does not change a decision
senses.definitionCN: 小到不会改变决策的支出
senses.example: The extra licence fee is trivial next to the legal risk.
senses.exampleCN: 与法律风险相比，额外的许可费微不足道。
senses.why: Costs are trivial when the decision would be the same without them.
senses.whyCN: 成本在去掉它决策也不变时，就是微不足道的。

senses.title: The obvious solution in mathematics
senses.definition: the simple solution that satisfies the equation without special work, often zero
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别处理即满足方程的简单解，常为零
senses.example: The equation has a trivial solution at zero and two others that matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个位于零的平凡解，另有两个真正重要的解。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for the case that gives itself away, which is the technical descendant of commonplace.
senses.whyCN: 数学用它指那个自己送上门的情形，是「平常」这一义的技术后裔。

senses.title: An objection that misses the point
senses.definition: a complaint that does not touch the main question
senses.definitionCN: 没有触及主要问题的抱怨
senses.example: He raised a trivial objection about the font and said nothing about the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他对字体提了个无关紧要的反对，对数据却一言不发。
senses.why: An objection is trivial when it leaves the main claim standing.
senses.whyCN: 反对在主要主张仍然立得住时，就是无关紧要的。

senses.title: Small details used to avoid the issue
senses.definition: minor points brought up to delay or distract
senses.definitionCN: 用细小的点来拖延或转移注意
senses.example: The report drowns in trivial details and never states the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 报告淹没在细枝末节里，始终没说清原因。
senses.why: Details become trivial when they are used to fill the space where the argument should be.
senses.whyCN: 当细节被用来填满本该放论证的位置，它们就成了细枝末节。

senses.title: Shallow talk
senses.definition: conversation without substance or interest
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质或趣味的谈话
senses.example: The party talk was trivial, but it passed the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上的谈话很浅薄，却也把晚上打发了。
senses.why: Talk without substance earns the word because it leaves nothing behind.
senses.whyCN: 没有实质的谈话得到这个词，因为它什么也没留下。

senses.title: A minor fault
senses.definition: an offence treated as slight rather than serious
senses.definitionCN: 被当作轻微而非严重的过错
senses.example: Under the old rules, a late form was a trivial offence with no penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧规，迟交表格属轻微过失，不受处罚。
senses.why: Law calls a fault trivial when the penalty is lighter than the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当处罚比文书手续还轻时，法律就把该过失称为轻微的。

senses.title: Too simple to need comment
senses.definition: so easy in computing or logic that it is not worth explaining
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机或逻辑上简单到不值得解释
senses.example: The remaining case is trivial, so the proof simply says it follows.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的情形简单到无需说明，证明里只写一句「由此可得」。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the oldest idea: so common and easy that it needs no remark.
senses.whyCN: 技术义保留了最古老的意思：太寻常、太容易，因而不必再提。

intro.en: Trivial comes from Latin trivialis, belonging to the crossroads, from trivium, a place where three roads meet. Medieval schools called the first three arts the trivium, so the adjective meant belonging to the basic studies, then commonplace, and finally of little importance. The modern sense grew out of that social judgement rather than from the number three.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「属于三岔路的」形容词，出自表示「三条路交汇处」的名词。中世纪学校把最初三门学科称为「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础学科的」，再变成「平常的」，最后成为「不重要的」。现代义从这种社会判断长出来，而不是从数字「三」直接得来。

items.en: A trivium was a place where three roads met, from tri- three and via road.
items.cn: 这个词指三条路交汇之处，由「三」与「道路」构成。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to such a public corner, hence common and ordinary.
items.cn: 该形容词指属于这种人流交汇的公共角落，因此有「平常、普通」之意。

items.en: The first three liberal arts were called the trivium, and trivialis came to mean belonging to basic instruction.
items.cn: 最初三门博雅学科合称「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础教学的」。

items.en: English took the word for things common and therefore slight.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于平常因而轻贱的事物。

items.en: The sense of unimportant hardened, and mathematics adopted it for the obvious case.
items.cn: 「不重要」义渐趋固定，数学又用它指显然的情形。

items.en: Quiz games and computing gave the word new phrases; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 问答游戏与计算机给出新的说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the crossroads root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of smallness. The note also ties trivial to its noun triviality.
note.cn: 第一组共享「三岔路」词根或形近；第二组指其他「小」的说法。这里也把形容词与其名词形式「琐碎」连起来。

entries.definition: The quality of being trivial, or a trivial thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指微不足道的性质，或一件琐事。

entries.definition: In a way that is easy or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指以轻易或不重要的方式。

entries.definition: To make something serious seem trivial.
entries.definitionCN: 指把严肃的事说得微不足道。

entries.definition: The three basic arts of the medieval curriculum.
entries.definitionCN: 指中世纪课程里的三门基础学科。

entries.definition: Small facts and unimportant details.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而无关紧要的事实与细节。

entries.definition: Hard labour or painful effort; it comes from a word for a three-pronged tool, not from the crossroads.
entries.definitionCN: 指艰苦劳作或痛苦努力；出自指三齿工具的词，与三岔路无关。

entries.definition: Too small to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到不值得考虑。

entries.definition: Small and unimportant, often said with a slight reproach.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而不重要，常带轻微责备。

entries.definition: Smaller in size, rank or importance than others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在规模、位次或重要性上较小。

entries.definition: So small that it can be ignored in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到实践中可以忽略。

entries.definition: Small-minded or concerned with small matters.
entries.definitionCN: 指心胸窄或只在意小事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the crossroads, the basic school subjects, the meeting that argues about wording, and the obvious equation case.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用三岔路口、基础学科、为一个用词争吵的会议，以及显然的方程情形。

normal.en: A crossroads is public and common, and common things soon look small.
normal.cn: 三岔路是公共而平常的，而平常的东西很快就显得微小。

normal.en: The three basic arts were the trivium, so trivial once meant elementary, not worthless.
normal.cn: 三门基础学科合称三艺，所以这个词曾经意为「基础的」，而不是「无价值的」。

normal.en: A trivial solution is the one that offers itself without effort.
normal.cn: 平凡解就是那个不用费力自己送上门的解。

normal.en: A trivial objection changes the font, not the argument.
normal.cn: 无关紧要的反对改的是字体，不是论证。

normal.en: Triviality is what happens when a serious subject is discussed only in small details.
normal.cn: 琐碎化，就是严肃话题只剩细枝末节时发生的事。

abstract.en: Calling something trivial is a way of deciding what will not be looked at.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为微不足道，是在决定什么不必再看。

abstract.en: The crossroads made a word for the common, and the common became a verdict on worth.
abstract.cn: 「三岔路」造出了一个表示「平常」的词，而「平常」又变成了对价值的判决。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a set of trivial cases, and they are the ones that teach the shape of the rest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都留着一批平凡情形，而正是它们教人看清其余部分的形状。

examples.en: The difference in price is trivial compared with the difference in quality.
examples.cn: 与质量差距相比，价格差距微不足道。

examples.en: Do not waste the meeting on trivial details that the report already covers.
examples.cn: 别把会议浪费在报告里已经写到的细枝末节上。

examples.en: The first case is trivial, so the proof moves straight to the second.
examples.cn: 第一种情形简单到无需说明，所以证明直接转向第二种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹尾偶」：三岔路口人来人往，人人都聊的「小事」，风一「吹」就散了

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「三岔路口」的名词，由「三」与「道路」构成，派生形容词义为「属于三岔路的、平常的」。中世纪把三门基础学科合称三艺，于是又指「基础学科的」，再演变为「平常的」，最后成为「微不足道的」。数学「平凡解」义为十九世纪后的技术引申；各短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the crossroads to the equation: unimportant, an everyday trifle, a negligible cost, the obvious mathematical case, a pointless objection, distracting details, shallow talk, a slight fault, and the simple case that needs no comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从三岔路走到方程：不重要、日常琐事、可忽略的成本、数学的显然情形、无的放矢的反对、转移注意的细节、浅薄的闲谈、轻微过失，以及无需说明的简单情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one end of the table is covered with notes about wording, while the budget sheet stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子一端堆满改词的纸条，另一端的预算表始终没有翻开。

branches.en: THE SMALL AMOUNT: importance and cost measured and found tiny.
branches.cn: 微小的分量：重要性与成本一量就小。

branches.en: THE TRIFLE AND THE DISTRACTION: small items, and small items used to avoid the point.
branches.cn: 琐事与分神：小东西，以及被用来回避要点的小东西。

branches.en: THE EASY CASE: the solution or case that offers itself.
branches.cn: 轻易的情形：自己送上门的解或情形。

branches.en: THE LIGHT COMPLAINT: an objection or fault too slight to matter.
branches.cn: 轻微的抱怨：轻到不必计较的反对或过失。

branches.en: THE SHALLOW TALK: conversation without substance.
branches.cn: 浅薄的谈话：没有实质的闲聊。

intro.en: Trivial is a crossroads noun with an adjective ending; the family covers trivia, the three basic arts, and the act of making something seem small.
intro.cn: 这个词是「三岔路」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖冷知识、三门基础学科，以及「把某事说得微不足道」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin tri- and via build trivium, and the derived adjective trivialis supplies the English word and its whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「三」与「道路」构成表示「三岔路」的名词，派生形容词给出英语词及其整个词族。

items.example: It marks the meeting of three roads.
It is also the source of English via.
items.exampleCN: 它也是英语「经由」的来源。

items.example: The noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族背后的名词。
它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
The plural keeps the idea of many small things.
items.exampleCN: 复数保留了「许多小东西」的意思。

由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地」

definition_zh: 持不同政见者；异见分子；持异见的
definition_en: a person who publicly disagrees with an established authority, especially a government
core_image: 一间小公寓的灯亮到深夜，桌上摊着被划满红线的报纸，主人把文稿塞进信封
scene: 墙上的广播一遍遍重复同一条消息，他关掉了开关。 The dissident kept writing anyway.
sceneCN: 这里 dissident 指持不同政见者（第 1 个义项：与当权者公开意见相左的人）；句意为这位异见者仍继续写作。

pos.zh: 持不同政见者
持异见的；不赞同的

senses.title: One who disagrees publicly
senses.definition: a person who states disagreement with an authority in public
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达与权威意见相左的人
senses.example: The dissident kept writing anyway.
senses.exampleCN: 这位异见者仍继续写作。
senses.why: The word names a person, not a mood: disagreement made visible and repeated.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是人，不是情绪：被看见、被重复的分歧。

senses.title: A voice inside a group
senses.definition: someone whose objection arises within an institution rather than outside it
senses.definitionCN: 在机构内部而非外部产生异议的人
senses.example: The party expelled its own dissident members.
senses.exampleCN: 该党开除了自己的异见成员。
senses.why: A dissident is most dangerous to a group when the disagreement comes from inside the house.
senses.whyCN: 当分歧来自屋里时，异见者对团体最危险。

senses.title: A political opponent
senses.definition: a citizen who opposes the policies or claims of a ruling power
senses.definitionCN: 反对执政者政策或主张的公民
senses.example: The regime jailed the leading dissident for ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 该政权把主要异见者判了十年监禁。
senses.why: Here the word becomes political shorthand: the disagreement is with the state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这里的词变成政治简称：分歧的对象是国家本身。

senses.title: A religious nonconformist
senses.definition: a believer who refuses an official doctrine or church order
senses.definitionCN: 拒绝官方教义或教会命令的信徒
senses.example: The dissident priest was removed from his parish.
senses.exampleCN: 这位持异见的牧师被免去了教区职务。
senses.why: Long before politics, the word described those who would not sign a creed.
senses.whyCN: 远在政治之前，这个词描述的是拒绝签署信条的人。

senses.title: A writer in exile
senses.definition: an author whose work is banned at home and continues abroad
senses.definitionCN: 作品在本国被禁、在国外继续写作的作者
senses.example: The dissident published her memoir in another country.
senses.exampleCN: 这位异见作家在另一个国家出版了回忆录。
senses.why: Exile turns disagreement into a place: the writing continues, the audience changes.
senses.whyCN: 流亡把分歧变成一个地点：写作继续，读者换了。

senses.title: Adjective: holding dissent
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean that the person or group dissents
senses.definitionCN: 用于名词前，表示该人或团体持异议
senses.example: A dissident faction split from the ruling party.
senses.exampleCN: 一个异见派系从执政党中分裂出去。
senses.why: Here the word stops naming a person and starts labelling a whole group by its disagreement.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词不再指一个人，而是用「有异议」给整个团体贴标签。

senses.title: An internal critic
senses.definition: a member who criticises the group in order to improve or change it
senses.definitionCN: 为改进或改变团体而批评它的成员
senses.example: She played the dissident at every board meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在每次董事会上都扮演内部批评者的角色。
senses.why: This sense carries loyalty inside the objection: the critic wants the group to survive.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项在异议里带着忠诚：批评者希望团体活下去。

senses.title: A movement of dissent
senses.definition: a loose network of people whose shared objection becomes organised
senses.definitionCN: 共同异议组织化后形成的松散网络
senses.example: The dissident movement grew quietly in the universities.
senses.exampleCN: 异见运动在大学里悄然壮大。
senses.why: Once individual voices find each other, the word shifts from person to current.
senses.whyCN: 当个体的声音彼此找到，这个词就从人转向潮流。

intro.en: Dissident is built from a prefix meaning apart and a verb meaning to sit, so it literally means sitting apart.
intro.cn: dissident 由一个意为「分开」的前缀和一个意为「坐」的动词构成，字面就是「分开坐」。

items.en: English took the adjective from Latin in the 16c., first for religious disagreement.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪从拉丁语借入这个形容词，最初用于宗教分歧。

items.en: Dissidere meant 'to sit apart, to disagree', as two people who will not share a bench.
items.cn: dissidere 意为「分开坐、意见不合」，像两个人不愿共用一条长凳。

items.en: Sedere 'to sit' also gives sediment and session, all about settling into place.
items.cn: sedere「坐」也给出 sediment 与 session，都与落到某处有关。

items.en: Dis- means apart; the sitting apart is the whole image of disagreement.
items.cn: dis- 意为分开；「分开坐」正是意见不合的整个画面。

items.en: In the 20c. the noun narrowed toward political opposition, especially under authoritarian rule.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个名词收窄为政治反对，尤其在威权统治之下。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sitting root; the near-meaning group lays out degrees of disagreement.
note.cn: 形近组共享「坐」的词根；近义组排列出分歧的各个程度。

entries.definition: the state or act of disagreeing with authority.
entries.definitionCN: 与权威意见相左的状态或行为。

entries.definition: in a manner that shows disagreement.
entries.definitionCN: 以显示异议的方式。

entries.definition: one who disagrees, especially with an official church.
entries.definitionCN: 持异议者，尤指不服从官方教会者。

entries.definition: an action that harms instead of helping.
entries.definitionCN: 帮倒忙的行为。

entries.definition: the expression of disagreement with a majority or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 对多数或权威表达不同意。

entries.definition: a person who publicly demonstrates against a policy.
entries.definitionCN: 公开针对某项政策示威的人。

entries.definition: a person who fights against an established power.
entries.definitionCN: 与既有权力斗争的人。

entries.definition: a person who will not follow established customs or doctrines.
entries.definitionCN: 不遵循既定习俗或教义的人。

normalIntro.en: The hooks hold on to the picture of a person deliberately sitting on a separate bench.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的联想留住「一个人故意坐到另一条长凳上」的画面。

normal.en: Dissident contains sed, to sit: the dissident sits apart.
normal.cn: dissident 含 sed（坐）：异见者坐到别处。

normal.en: Two s sounds at the start: dis-si-dent, like a hiss of refusal.
normal.cn: 开头连着两个 s 音：dis-si-dent，像一声拒绝的嘶气。

normal.en: Think of a lone chair moved to the back of the hall.
normal.cn: 想象一把孤零零的椅子被搬到会场最后面。

normal.en: Link with sediment: both settle, one to the bottom, one to the edge.
normal.cn: 和 sediment 联系：两者都落定，一个沉底，一个落到边缘。

normal.en: The adjective and noun look the same; only the article tells you which is which.
normal.cn: 形容词和名词长得一样；只有冠词告诉你哪个是哪个。

abstract.en: Disagreement becomes identity when it is spoken often enough in public.
abstract.cn: 当分歧在公众面前被说得足够多，它就变成身份。

abstract.en: A dissident keeps the group honest, which is why groups rarely thank them.
abstract.cn: 异见者让团体保持诚实，因此团体很少感谢他们。

abstract.en: Sitting apart is not leaving; the dissident is still in the room.
abstract.cn: 分开坐不等于离开；异见者仍在这间屋里。

examples.en: The dissident kept writing anyway.
examples.cn: 这位异见者仍继续写作。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from a single act of sitting apart to a whole movement, first religious, then political, then organised.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项从「分开坐」这一个动作，扩展到一个完整的运动，先宗教，再政治，最后组织化。

core.en: SITTING APART IN THE SAME ROOM

branches.en: The single person who objects, inside or outside the group.
branches.cn: 提出异议的那一个人，无论团体内外。

branches.en: Opposition organised against a state, including exile.
branches.cn: 针对国家组织起来的反对，包括流亡。

branches.en: The older religious sense of refusing a creed.
branches.cn: 较古老的宗教意义：拒绝信条。

branches.en: The same word used as an adjective before a noun.
branches.cn: 同一个词用作名词前的形容词。

branches.en: Individual voices joining into a visible movement.

intro.en: The sed family is about sitting and settling: dissident sits apart, resident sits back, president sits before.
intro.cn: sed 词族与坐和落定有关：dissident 分开坐，resident 坐回去，president 坐在前面。

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 给每个成员一个座位；前缀说明这个「坐」发生在哪里。
