definition_zh: 交往；与人相处；使适应社会规范；使公有化、集体化
definition_en: to meet and spend time with other people in a friendly way, or to train someone to fit into a group
core_image: 一个人先被带去吃午饭，再被拉去周末清扫，点头逐渐变成熟识，最后能与整条街的人自然打招呼
scene: 这里指「交往」。 New employees socialize over lunch and weekend clean-ups until the whole block knows them.
sceneCN: 此处指「在工作之外与人相处、逐渐熟识」（第 1 个义项：以轻松方式与他人交往）；句意为新员工借午餐与周末清扫同大家交往，直到整条街都认识他们。可辨识物件：长餐桌、清扫工具、街区巷道、门牌与笑脸。

pos.zh: 交往；参加社交活动（不及物）
使适应社会规范；使学会群体生活（及物）
使公有化；使集体化（及物）

senses.title: To meet people socially
senses.titleCN: 与人交往、参加社交活动
senses.definition: to spend time with other people in a relaxed, friendly way, especially outside work
senses.definitionCN: 在工作之外以轻松友好的方式与他人共度时光
senses.example: New employees socialize over lunch and weekend clean-ups until the whole block knows them.
senses.exampleCN: 新员工借午餐与周末清扫同大家交往，直到整条街都认识他们。
senses.why: Social plus the verb ending -ize gives 'to make social' or 'to act socially'; the everyday sense is simply to take part in company.
senses.whyCN: social 加动词词尾 -ize 表示「使成为社会的」或「做社会性的事」，日常义就是参与交往。

senses.title: To train someone into a group
senses.definition: to bring a child or newcomer into the expected ways of a group through repeated guidance
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复引导，使儿童或新成员学会群体的期待行事方式
senses.example: The school socializes pupils into queues, bells and shared desks.
senses.exampleCN: 学校把学生训练成习惯排队、听铃声与共用课桌的人。
senses.why: The causative reading 'to make social' turned into 'to make fit for society', which is the base of the sociological noun.
senses.whyCN: 「使成为社会的」这一使动义转为「使适应社会」，这正是社会学名词的基础。

senses.title: To bring under collective ownership
senses.definition: to transfer land, industry or costs from private owners to public or shared control
senses.definitionCN: 把土地、产业或成本从私人所有者转归公共或共同控制
senses.example: The new government moved to socialize the railways within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 新政府上台一年内就着手把铁路公有化。
senses.why: If social means belonging to a community, then to socialize property means to make it belong to the community, a political extension of 'make social'.
senses.whyCN: 如果 social 指属于共同体，那么使财产社会化就是使其归共同体所有，这是「使成为社会的」在政治上的延伸。

senses.title: To introduce a newcomer
senses.definition: to help a new person enter a group by arranging introductions and shared activities
senses.definitionCN: 通过安排介绍与共同活动，帮助新来者进入群体
senses.example: A neighbour socialized the family by inviting them to the block party.
senses.exampleCN: 一位邻居邀请这家人参加街区聚会，使他们融入社区。
senses.why: Mixing is not only pleasure; it is also the act of bringing someone in, so the verb takes on this welcoming sense.
senses.whyCN: 交往不只是消遣，也是把某人带进来的动作，因此这个动词又带上迎接新人的意思。

senses.title: To turn an event into a social occasion
senses.titleCN: 使某项活动成为社交场合
senses.definition: to give an activity a friendly, conversational character rather than a purely practical one
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动带上友好交谈的性质，而非纯务实性质
senses.example: They socialized the dull committee meeting with coffee and introductions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用咖啡与自我介绍把沉闷的委员会会议变得像社交聚会。
senses.why: Because the verb means to make something social, it can describe changing the tone of an event, not only attending it.
senses.whyCN: 由于这个动词意为「使某事物具有社会性」，它可以描述改变活动气氛，而不只是出席。

senses.title: To shape behaviour through interaction
senses.definition: to shape a person's habits gradually through repeated contact with others
senses.definitionCN: 通过与他人的反复接触逐步塑造一个人的习惯
senses.example: Playground games socialize children into sharing rules without any formal lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 操场游戏不需要正式课程，就把孩子训练成懂得分享规则的人。
senses.why: This is the psychological side of training: behaviour is shaped by contact, not only by instruction.
senses.whyCN: 这是训练的心理侧面：行为由接触塑造，而不只由教导塑造。

senses.title: To make socially acceptable
senses.definition: to adjust a practice so that it fits accepted social norms
senses.definitionCN: 调整某项做法，使其符合被接受的社会规范
senses.example: The old ceremony was socialized into a public holiday rather than abandoned.
senses.exampleCN: 旧仪式被改造成公共节日而保留下来，并没有被废弃。
senses.why: Things as well as people can be made social, which is why the verb sometimes means bringing a practice into line with public norms.
senses.whyCN: 不只是人能社会化，事物也能，因此这个动词有时指使某项做法符合公共规范。

senses.title: To join group leisure
senses.definition: to take part in the leisure life of a group, such as dinners, games or outings
senses.definitionCN: 参加群体的休闲生活，如聚餐、游戏或郊游
senses.example: On Sundays the whole yard socializes around a long table of fruit and tea.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢星期天，整个院子都围着长桌吃水果喝茶，彼此交往。
senses.why: The narrow everyday reading focuses on leisure rather than training, and it is the sense most common in speech.
senses.whyCN: 这一窄化的日常义聚焦休闲而非训练，是口语中最常见的用法。

intro.en: Socialize is social plus the Greek-derived verb ending -ize. The verb was formed in English and later split into a friendly sense and a technical sense of training or public ownership. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: socialize 由 social 加希腊来源的动词词尾 -ize 构成。这个动词在英语中形成，后来分出「友好交往」与「训练或公有化」两类技术义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Socialis meant 'of companionship or alliance', from socius 'ally'. It reached English as social through Old French.
items.cn: socialis 意为「结伴或联盟的」，源于 socius「盟友」，经古法语进入英语作 social。

items.en: Greek -izein meant 'to make, to act, to cause'. English took it as -ize and used it freely with nouns and adjectives.
items.cn: 希腊 -izein 意为「使、做、造成」，英语借作 -ize，广泛接在名词与形容词后构词。

items.en: Socialize was formed in English on the adjective social, with the literal sense 'to make social'.
items.cn: socialize 是英语在形容词 social 基础上构成的，字面义为「使成为社会的」。

items.en: The literal sense developed into 'to make fit for society', which became the standard term in sociology and education.
items.cn: 字面义发展为「使适应社会」，并成为社会学与教育学的标准术语。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the same verb was applied to property, giving 'to bring into public ownership'.
items.cn: 在十九与二十世纪，同一个动词被用于财产，产生「转为公有」的意思。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English citation of socialize is not precisely dated, and the order in which its senses appeared is reconstructed from later records.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：socialize 的最早英语书证缺乏精确年代，各义项出现的先后顺序是根据较晚记录推定的。

note.en: Group one holds verbs built on the same social root or the same ending; group two holds verbs of joining that differ in tone or in purpose.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 social 词根或同带 -ize 词尾的动词；第二组是语气或目的不同的「加入」类动词。

entries.definition: The adjective for interaction or society; socialize is the verb formed from it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示交往或社会的形容词；socialize 是由它构成的动词。

entries.definition: Names the process that socialize describes in action.
entries.definitionCN: 指 socialize 所述动作的过程名词。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who easily joins others; it cannot replace the verb in 'socialize with'.
entries.definitionCN: 描述乐于与人相处的形容词，不能替换「与……交往」中的动词。

entries.definition: Means to make widely known; the ending is the same but the base is public, so the meaning is not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 意为使广为人知；词尾相同但词基是 public，因此词义并不相通。

entries.definition: To circulate among guests; it stresses movement and casual talk rather than becoming part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 在宾客间走动交谈；强调走动与闲聊，而非融入群体。

entries.definition: A general verb for combining or associating; socialize adds the friendly, group-life flavour.
entries.definitionCN: 结合或往来的通称；socialize 多一层友好群体生活的意味。

entries.definition: To act on one another, often in a studied or formal way; it need not be friendly leisure.
entries.definitionCN: 彼此施加作用，常用于研究或正式语境，不必是友好休闲。

entries.definition: To keep company with or connect oneself to a group, often with a formal or professional tone.
entries.definitionCN: 与某群体来往或建立联系，常带正式或职业语气。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Social plus -ize: the verb literally means to make social or to act in company.
normal.cn: social 加 -ize：动词字面义是「使成为社会的」或在人群中行动。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the sense: socialize with colleagues, socialize children, socialize costs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出词义：与同事交往、使孩子适应社会、使成本社会化。

normal.en: The family runs socialization, socialized, socializing, social and society.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 socialization、socialized、socializing、social 与 society。

normal.en: The same ending appears in organize, realize and publicize, but each base word sets its own meaning.
normal.cn: 同一词尾也见于 organize、realize 与 publicize，但每个词基决定各自的词义。

normal.en: The technical senses are marked by objects: you socialize children into rules, and you socialize an industry into public hands.
normal.cn: 技术义靠宾语分辨：使孩子学会规则，或使某行业转为公有。

abstract.en: Picture a newcomer standing at the edge of a room until someone pulls out the next chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一个新人站在屋子边缘，直到有人拉出旁边的椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a private gate being opened so that the whole lane may walk through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇私人的门被打开，让整条巷子的人都能穿行。

abstract.en: Picture two strangers slowly turning the same dull task into a conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象两个陌生人慢慢把同一件枯燥的事变成一场谈话。

examples.en: The department socializes on Friday afternoons, and nobody talks about work.
examples.cn: 这个部门每周五下午聚会交往，没人谈工作。

examples.en: Board games socialize children into waiting their turn.
examples.cn: 棋盘游戏让孩子学会轮流等待。

examples.en: The council moved to socialize waste collection across the district.
examples.cn: 议会着手把全区的垃圾收集转为公共管理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「social（社会的）+ ize（使……）」——使彼此变成熟人 → 交往；使适应社会 → 社会化

root: socialize 由 social 加希腊来源词尾 -ize 构成；social 出自拉丁 socialis，词根 socius「盟友」；-ize 出自希腊 -izein「使、做」。该动词在英语中形成，最早书证年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses split one verb in two directions: outward into friendly company and inward into training, then into ownership, welcome, tone, shaping, norms and plain leisure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把这个动词分成两个方向：向外是友好交往，向内是训练，再分出公有化、迎接、气氛、塑造、规范与单纯休闲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newcomer at the edge of a room, gradually pulled into its circle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个新人站在屋子边缘，逐渐被拉进圈子。

branches.en: FREE MIXING: the everyday sense is simply friendly company and group leisure.
branches.cn: 自由交往：日常义就是友好结伴与群体休闲。

branches.en: TRAINING: repeated contact and guidance turn a newcomer into a member.
branches.cn: 训练：反复接触与引导把新人变成成员。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: making something social becomes making it publicly held.
branches.cn: 所有权：使某物具有社会性，转为使其归公共所有。

branches.en: WELCOME AND TONE: one can bring a person in and can also change an event's mood.
branches.cn: 迎接与气氛：既能带人进来，也能改变活动的气氛。

branches.en: NORMATIVE FIT: even a practice can be adjusted to accepted public rules.
branches.cn: 规范适配：连一项做法也能被调整到符合公共规则。

intro.en: The verb joins an English adjective to a Greek verb ending, and its derived words keep the same -iz- spine.
intro.cn: 这个动词把英语形容词接到希腊动词词尾上，其派生词延续同一条 -iz- 词干。

latinIntro.en: Latin socius and socialis supply the base; Greek -izein supplies the ending that makes it a verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 socius 与 socialis 提供词基；希腊 -izein 提供使其成为动词的词尾。

items.example: The root names the people one joins.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指人所加入的人群。
孩子们很早就完成社会化。
这里的交往不占太多时间。
社会化在学校里被研究。

derivatives.meaningCN: 已社会化的；已公有化的

definition_zh: adj. 眩晕的；头晕的；令人眩晕的；眼花缭乱的；（旧）愚蠢的
definition_en: feeling that everything is spinning, causing that feeling, or too fast for the mind to follow
core_image: 一张脸在地板似乎倾斜时变得苍白；一部玻璃电梯一层层往上升；夜里一片模糊的霓虹招牌与穿行的车流；一个戴着纸王冠咧嘴笑的宫廷弄臣
scene: 她起身太快，地板好像斜了过来，脸一下子白了。 She felt dizzy when she stood up too fast.
sceneCN: 这里 dizzy 是「眩晕的」（第 1 个义项：觉得自己或房间在旋转）；句意：她起身太快，觉得一阵眩晕。图中可辨识物件：椅子、倾斜的地板、苍白的脸、扶住桌沿的手。

pos.zh: 眩晕的；头晕的；令人眩晕的；眼花缭乱的

senses.title: Feeling the spin
senses.definition: having the feeling that you or the room is turning round
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）觉得自己或房间在旋转的
senses.example: She felt dizzy when she stood up too fast.
senses.exampleCN: 她起身太快，觉得一阵眩晕。
senses.why: A face going pale as the floor seems to lean.
senses.whyCN: 一张脸在地板似乎倾斜时变得苍白。

senses.title: Making you unsteady
senses.definition: causing people to feel unsteady or giddy
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）使人站不稳或头晕的
senses.example: The dizzy height of the tower frightened the visitors.
senses.exampleCN: 塔楼令人眩晕的高度吓住了游客。
senses.why: A glass lift rising past floor after floor.
senses.whyCN: 一部玻璃电梯一层层往上升。

senses.title: Too fast to follow
senses.definition: so fast or busy that the mind cannot keep up
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）快到或忙到脑子跟不上的
senses.example: The dizzy pace of the city wore her out.
senses.exampleCN: 城市令人眼花缭乱的节奏把她累垮了。
senses.why: A blur of neon signs and crossing traffic at night.
senses.whyCN: 夜里一片模糊的霓虹招牌与穿行的车流。

senses.title: Silly in older use
senses.definition: foolish or stupid, in older English
senses.definitionCN: （形容词）在旧式英语里指愚蠢的
senses.example: The old tale calls the prince a dizzy youth.
senses.exampleCN: 那个老故事称王子是个傻小子。
senses.why: A grinning court jester wearing a paper crown.
senses.whyCN: 一个戴着纸王冠、咧嘴笑的宫廷弄臣。

intro.en: Dizzy descends from Old English dysig, foolish; a muddled head and a spinning head felt like the same thing, so by the sixteenth century the word had turned to giddy.
intro.cn: dizzy 源自古英语 dysig「愚蠢」；糊涂的脑袋与旋转的脑袋感觉像是同一回事，所以到十六世纪这个词已转成「头晕」。

items.en: Old English dysig meant foolish or stupid.
items.cn: 古英语 dysig 意为愚蠢的。

items.en: Middle English dizy still meant foolish.
items.cn: 中古英语 dizy 仍意为愚蠢的。

items.en: The sense shifts from foolish to giddy.
items.cn: 词义从「愚蠢」转向「头晕」。

items.en: Dizzy comes to describe heights that make you unsteady.
items.cn: dizzy 转而形容使人站不稳的高度。

items.en: Dizzy also describes a pace too fast to follow.
items.cn: dizzy 也形容快到跟不上的节奏。

note.en: Dizzy is a spinning head; its look-alikes share the stem or the idea of stunned senses, and its neighbours name nearby kinds of unsteadiness.
note.cn: dizzy 是旋转的脑袋；形近词共用词干或「感官发懵」的意思，近义词则是相近的几种站不稳。

intro.cn: dizzy 用 -er 与 -est 构成比较级和最高级，用 -ness 构成状态名词，用 -ily 构成副词；拉丁语「转」的词根 vert- 提供了表亲 vertigo。

definition_zh: 时间的；时间先后上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的；（解剖）颞的
definition_en: relating to time or to the order of events, and, in another line of the same spelling, relating to temples of the head or to worldly affairs
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉按年份一层层往下排，同一件事的三份记录落在三个不同的格子里
scene: 档案室里，三份记录同一事件的文件夹按年份排成一列，谁在前谁在后一眼可见。 Researchers tracked the temporal order of the three events rather than the distance between them.
sceneCN: 这里指事件在时间上的先后（第 2 个义项：时间先后次序）；句意为研究者追踪三个事件的时间先后，而不是它们之间的空间距离。图中可辨识物件：按年份排列的档案夹、三份记录、年份标签、档案柜。

pos.zh: 时间的；时间上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的
（解剖）颞的；太阳穴部位的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上；按时间」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性；暂时性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
解剖学中由同一部位名词构成的名称，指颞肌
由表示「在上」的前缀加该解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

senses.title: Relating to time
senses.definition: concerned with time as a dimension
senses.definitionCN: 涉及时间这一维度的
senses.example: The study measures temporal change rather than differences between places.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量的是随时间发生的变化，而不是地方之间的差异。
senses.why: The Latin word for time gives this adjective its broadest frame, and most other senses narrow it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「时间」的词给出最宽的框架，其余义项大多是在此之上收窄。

senses.title: Order of events in time
senses.definition: the sequence in which events happen
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生的先后顺序
senses.example: The notes record the temporal order of the symptoms, not their severity.
senses.exampleCN: 记录写的是症状出现的时间先后，而不是轻重。
senses.why: Order needs an axis, and time supplies one; this sense is the everyday core.
senses.whyCN: 次序需要一个轴，时间提供了这个轴，这是最日常的核心义。

senses.title: Time resolution
senses.definition: how finely an instrument or dataset divides time
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或数据集把时间切分的精细程度
senses.example: The camera's temporal resolution is one frame every ten milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机的时间分辨率是每十毫秒一帧。
senses.why: Here time is measured as a grid, so the word marks the fineness of that grid.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间被当成一张网格来量，词于是标出网格的细密程度。

senses.title: The temporal lobe of the brain
senses.definition: the lobe at the side of the head, named from the temples
senses.definitionCN: 位于头侧、因太阳穴部位得名的脑叶
senses.example: The temporal lobe handles much of what we hear and remember.
senses.exampleCN: 颞叶负责我们所听到与记住的很大一部分内容。
senses.why: This sense belongs to a different Latin word, the plural name for the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项属于另一个拉丁词，即「头部太阳穴」的复数形式。

senses.title: Worldly power
senses.definition: authority over worldly affairs as opposed to spiritual authority
senses.definitionCN: 对世俗事务的管辖权，与属灵权力相对
senses.example: The dispute was over temporal power, not over doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 争论针对的是世俗权力，而不是教义。
senses.why: The church set the authority of this world against the authority of the next, and the word carried the contrast.
senses.whyCN: 教会把此世的权力与彼世的权力对立起来，这个词就承载了这组对照。

senses.title: Earthly and passing
senses.definition: belonging to this world and therefore not lasting
senses.definitionCN: 属于此世、因而不能长久的
senses.example: Monks renounced temporal goods but kept their books.
senses.exampleCN: 修士舍弃尘世的财物，却留下了书。
senses.why: The same axis of time carries a judgement: what is in time will pass.
senses.whyCN: 同一条时间轴带上了判断：凡在时间之中的都会过去。

senses.title: A clause of time
senses.definition: a subordinate clause saying when something happens
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事何时发生的从属分句
senses.example: The sentence opens with a temporal clause introduced by after.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子以表示「之后」的连接词引导的时间从句开头。
senses.why: Grammar names by function, so any clause marking time takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 语法按功能命名，凡标出时间的分句都用这个形容词。

senses.title: Temporal scale
senses.definition: the length of time over which something is observed
senses.definitionCN: 观察某事所跨的时间长度
senses.example: Climate and soil form on very different temporal scales.
senses.exampleCN: 气候与土壤在以极为不同的时间尺度形成。
senses.why: Scale is the length of the ruler, and on the time axis the ruler is a span of years.
senses.whyCN: 尺度就是尺子的长度；放在时间轴上，这把尺子就是一段年份。

intro.en: Temporal is two words wearing one shape. The time sense comes from Latin tempus, time, and its adjective temporalis, which also supplied the church's word for worldly affairs. The anatomy sense comes from Latin tempora, the temples of the head, a different word. English merged them in spelling, not in origin.
intro.cn: 这个词其实是两个词穿了同一件外衣。时间义来自拉丁语 tempus「时间」及其形容词，教会又用它指世俗事务。解剖义来自拉丁语 tempora「头部太阳穴」，是另一个词。英语只是在拼写上把它们合在一起，来源并不相同。

items.en: Tempus meant time, with the stem tempor- appearing in all other cases.
items.cn: 这个词意为「时间」，其余各格都用表示「时间」的词干。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to time, and the church used it for what belongs to this world.
items.cn: 该形容词意为「属于时间的」，教会用它指属于此世的事物。

items.en: A separate noun, plural of tempus in the sense of the temples of the head, gave the anatomical word.
items.cn: 另一个名词，即「太阳穴」义的复数，给出了解剖学上的这个词。

items.en: French kept the church contrast between the worldly and the spiritual.
items.cn: 法语保留了教会关于「世俗」与「属灵」的对照。

items.en: English took both senses, and later added the grammatical and scientific uses.
items.cn: 英语把两个义项都吸收进来，后来又加上语法与科学用法。

items.en: Measurement and neuroscience gave the word new compounds; the first dates of those compounds are uncertain.
items.cn: 测量与神经科学又给出新的复合说法；这些说法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the time root or looks close; the second group names time, worldliness and related ideas. The note also contrasts temporal with spatial, and separates the time sense from the anatomy sense.
note.cn: 第一组共享「时间」词根或形近；第二组指时间、世俗及相关概念。这里也把「时间的」与「空间的」对照说清，并分开时间义与解剖义。

entries.definition: Lasting only for a time; the same time root with an ending meaning lasting for a period.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续一段时间；同一时间词根加表示「持续一段」的词尾。

entries.definition: For a limited time only.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅在有限时间内。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from the Italian use of the time word.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐的速度，来自意大利语对「时间」一词的使用。

entries.definition: Existing at the same time; the prefix means with.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在的；前缀意为「共同」。

entries.definition: To stall or act evasively in order to gain time.
entries.definitionCN: 指为争取时间而拖延或见风使舵。

entries.definition: Relating to space, the other axis of measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与空间有关，是测量所用的另一条轴。

entries.definition: Arranged by date, with explicit times attached.
entries.definitionCN: 指按日期排列，并明确标出时间。

entries.definition: Concerned with this world rather than with religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指关心此世而非宗教事务。

entries.definition: Concerned with material life and its affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 指关注物质生活及其事务。

entries.definition: Lasting only a short time and then gone.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续很短时间便消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the dated file drawers, the framework of the church, the temple-side lobe and the frame rate of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按年份排的档案抽屉、教会与世俗的对照、头侧的脑叶以及相机的帧率。

normal.en: Temporal questions ask when, the mirror of spatial questions asking where.
normal.cn: 时间类问题问「什么时候」，正好映照空间类问题的「在哪里」。

normal.en: A temporal clause is a subordinate sentence that answers when.
normal.cn: 时间从句就是回答「何时」的从属句。

normal.en: The temporal lobe sits beside the temples, which is exactly what its Latin name says.
normal.cn: 颞叶位于太阳穴旁，它的拉丁名称说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Temporal power is the church's word for the authority of this world.
normal.cn: 世俗权力是教会用来指此世权威的说法。

normal.en: Temporal scale decides what looks fast and what looks slow.
normal.cn: 时间尺度决定什么看起来快、什么看起来慢。

abstract.en: Time is the axis that makes order visible, and this adjective is the name of that axis.
abstract.cn: 时间是把次序变可见的那条轴，而这个形容词就是这条轴的名字。

abstract.en: Two unrelated Latin nouns ended up with the same English spelling, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 两个互不相干的拉丁名词最后拼成了一个英语单词，只能靠上下文分开。

abstract.en: Anything inside time is already leaving, which is why the worldly sense carries a hint of loss.
abstract.cn: 凡在时间之中的都已开始离去，所以世俗义总带一丝失去的意味。

examples.en: The two records differ in temporal order but agree on content.
examples.cn: 这两份记录在时间先后上不同，内容却一致。

examples.en: Temporal power and spiritual authority were once argued in the same courtroom.
examples.cn: 世俗权力与属灵权威曾在一间法庭上被同时争辩。

examples.en: Fossils and languages change on completely different temporal scales.
examples.cn: 化石与语言以完全不同的时间尺度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦泼若」：先问「时间」什么时候到，再问「尘土」什么时候散，一事一时都记在案上

root: 一支源于拉丁语中表示「时间」的名词及其形容词，教会又引申指「世俗的」；另一支源于拉丁语中表示「头部太阳穴」的复数名词，给出解剖学的「颞的」。两支同形异源，英语只在拼写上合并。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use two roots: time, its order, its resolution and scale; the anatomy of the temples; worldly power and worldly transience; and the grammar of when.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个词根：时间本身、时间次序、时间分辨率与时间尺度；太阳穴部位的解剖；世俗权力与尘世短暂；以及表示「何时」的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three folders for one event slide into year-labelled drawers, and the order is visible at a glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一事件的三份档案滑进标着年份的抽屉，先后一眼可见。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND ITS ORDER: time as a dimension, then events placed along it.
branches.cn: 轴与轴上的次序：先是时间这一维度，再是沿它摆放的事件。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SPAN: fine resolution at one end, long scale at the other.
branches.cn: 被丈量的跨度：一端是精细分辨率，一端是长尺度。

branches.en: THE TEMPLES' LOBE: a second Latin root hiding under the same spelling.
branches.cn: 太阳穴的脑叶：同一拼写之下藏着第二个拉丁词根。

branches.en: THE WORLD AND ITS PASSING: authority here, and the fact that it fades.
branches.cn: 此世与其消逝：这里的权力，以及它终将褪去。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE OF WHEN: grammar marking time in a sentence.
branches.cn: 「何时」从句：语法在句中标出时间。

intro.en: Temporal is a Latin time noun with an adjective ending; its family covers lasting for a time, the musical tempo, and the anatomy of the temples.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「时间」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖「暂时的」、音乐的速度，以及太阳穴的解剖。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus and its stem tempor- supply the time line, while the plural tempora supplies the anatomy line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「时间」及其词干提供时间这一线，而复数形式「太阳穴」提供解剖这一线。

items.example: The source of the time sense.
The stem seen in temporal and temporary.
items.exampleCN: 见于「时间的」与「暂时的」两词。
它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: A separate word behind the anatomy sense.
items.exampleCN: 解剖义背后是另一个词。

items.example: It marks both senses as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 它把两个义项都标为形容词。

items.example: It forms temporary, lasting for a time.

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
由表示「在上」的前缀加解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

definition_zh: 灾难性的；毁灭性的；造成彻底失败的
definition_en: causing or involving ruin on a very large scale
core_image: 一排多米诺骨牌从第一张开始连锁倒下，最后一张砸穿了地板
scene: 洪水退去后，粮仓只剩空架，农会估计损失足以让全镇破产，形容为灾难性后果。 When the floodwater withdrew, only the empty frame of the granary remained, and the farm board called the losses catastrophic enough to bankrupt the whole town.
sceneCN: 这里 catastrophic 指「造成大范围、近乎不可挽回的破坏」（第 1 个义项：后果具毁灭性）；句意为洪水退去后粮仓只剩空架，农会称损失之大足以让全镇破产。可辨识物件：空粮仓骨架、倒伏的骨牌、泡水的账册、破堤口。

pos.zh: 灾难性的；毁灭性的（多作定语，也可作表语）

senses.title: Causing ruin on a large scale
senses.definition: causing destruction that is widespread and hard to reverse
senses.definitionCN: 造成广泛且难以逆转的破坏
senses.example: The storm surge had a catastrophic effect on the low-lying districts.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴潮对低洼城区造成了灾难性影响。
senses.why: the adjective simply carries the noun's overturning into a modifier: whatever it touches is turned over.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把名词的「翻转」带进修饰位置：它触到的东西都被掀翻。

senses.title: Disastrous as an outcome
senses.definition: ending in complete and damaging failure
senses.definitionCN: 以彻底且有害的失败告终
senses.example: The decision to ignore the engineers proved catastrophic.
senses.exampleCN: 无视工程师意见的决定被证明是灾难性的。
senses.why: nothing physical is destroyed here; what collapses is the plan and the trust behind it.
senses.whyCN: 这里没有实物被毁，崩塌的是计划以及支撑计划的信任。

senses.title: Involving enormous financial loss
senses.definition: producing losses so large that they threaten the survival of the organisation
senses.definitionCN: 造成的损失之大，危及组织本身的存续
senses.example: Insurers class a single storm as catastrophic once claims pass a fixed threshold.
senses.exampleCN: 一旦赔款超过固定门槛，保险公司就把单场风暴列为灾难性事件。
senses.why: the insurance industry turned the adjective into a threshold label for losses that break a balance sheet.
senses.whyCN: 保险业把这个形容词变成门槛标签，专指足以击穿资产负债表的损失。

senses.title: Of a drama's final reversal
senses.definition: belonging to the closing reversal in which a tragedy's fortunes are destroyed
senses.definitionCN: 属于悲剧命运被彻底毁掉的收场转折
senses.example: The playwright keeps the catastrophic scene off stage and reports it in a messenger's speech.
senses.exampleCN: 剧作家把这一灾难性的场面留在幕后，由传信人的台词转述。
senses.why: drama criticism kept the technical sense, using the adjective for the moment when the reversal lands.
senses.whyCN: 戏剧评论保留了这一专门义，用该形容词指逆转落地的那一刻。

senses.title: Of a sudden geological upheaval
senses.definition: describing a sudden worldwide change in the earth's crust or climate
senses.definitionCN: 描述地壳或气候的突然全球性变化
senses.example: Catastrophic eruptions can cool the whole planet for a year.
senses.exampleCN: 灾难性的火山喷发能让整个行星降温一年。
senses.why: geology needed a word for change by sudden event rather than slow accumulation, and borrowed this one.
senses.whyCN: 地质学需要一个词指「由突发事件造成的变化」而非缓慢累积，于是借用了它。

senses.title: Severe and irreversible in medicine
senses.titleCN: 医学上严重且不可逆的
senses.definition: describing an illness or injury that is severe, sudden and permanently damaging
senses.definitionCN: 描述严重、突发且造成永久损害的疾病或损伤
senses.example: The policy covers catastrophic illness but not routine care.
senses.exampleCN: 这份保单覆盖重大疾病，但不含日常诊疗。
senses.why: medicine borrowed the financial threshold label: the illness is catastrophic because of its cost and permanence, not its cause.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了财务门槛标签：疾病之所以「灾难性」，在于费用与不可逆，而非成因。

senses.title: Of an abrupt jump in a system
senses.definition: describing a discontinuous change in which a small shift produces a large jump
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种不连续变化：微小移动带来巨大跳变
senses.example: The model predicts a catastrophic jump once the load passes the fold point.
senses.exampleCN: 模型预测，一旦荷载越过折点，就会出现灾难性跳变。
senses.why: catastrophe theory used the word for the fold in a surface, so the adjective marks the jump itself.
senses.whyCN: 突变理论用这个词指曲面上的折处，因此形容词标记的是跳变本身。

senses.title: Abstract: overwhelmingly harmful
senses.definition: used loosely for anything felt to be overwhelmingly harmful or badly judged
senses.definitionCN: 宽泛地用于任何被认为极其有害或判断极糟的事物
senses.example: Calling the merger catastrophic was an exaggeration, but the lost jobs were real.
senses.exampleCN: 把这次合并称为灾难性有些夸张，但失去的工作岗位是真的。
senses.why: the loose use keeps only the intensity of the original: something is judged as if it had been overturned.
senses.whyCN: 宽泛用法只保留原词的强度：某事物被判定得仿佛被掀翻过一样。

intro.en: Catastrophic is the adjective of catastrophe, the Greek katastrophē 'overturning', plus the Greek adjectival ending -ikos. It reached English through Latin and French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: catastrophic 是大灾难 catastrophe 的形容词，由希腊 katastrophē「翻转」加希腊形容词词尾 -ikos 构成，经拉丁语与法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Katastrophē 'an overturning' came from kata- 'down' plus strephein 'to turn'; the deeper origin of strephein is not established.
items.cn: katastrophē「翻转」由 kata-「向下」加 strephein「转」构成；strephein 的更远来源未得到证明。

items.en: -ikos was the ordinary Greek ending for 'belonging to, of the nature of', so katastrophikos meant 'of an overturning'.
items.cn: -ikos 是希腊语中表示「属于、具有……性质」的常用词尾，因此 katastrophikos 意为「翻转性质的」。

items.en: Latin -icus and French -ique carried the ending into English -ic, which by the seventeenth century attached freely to nouns of Greek origin.
items.cn: 拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 把这个词尾带入英语 -ic，到 17 世纪它已能自由附着于希腊来源的名词。

items.en: Catastrophic appears in English drama criticism before it spreads to ordinary description of floods, wars and failures.
items.cn: catastrophic 先出现在英语戏剧评论中，之后才扩展到对洪水、战争与失败的日常描述。

items.en: Insurance fixed catastrophic loss as a threshold term, and medicine followed with catastrophic illness; geology used it in the catastrophism debate.
items.cn: 保险业把 catastrophic loss 定为门槛术语，医学随后有 catastrophic illness；地质学在灾变论之争中也使用了它。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of strephein is unsettled, and no exact first citation is recorded for the insurance sense, so the dates given are approximations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：strephein 在希腊语之前的历史未定，保险义也没有确切的最早书证，所给年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds adjectives that differ in what they blame or how final the harm is; group two holds the nouns and adverbs that share the same root.
note.cn: 第一组是归因或终结程度不同的形容词；第二组是同根的名词与副词。

entries.definition: Built on Greek klyzein 'to wash', so it stresses a flood-like physical rush rather than a whole order overturned.
entries.definitionCN: 由希腊 klyzein「冲洗」构成，强调洪水般的物理冲击，而非整套秩序被翻转。

entries.definition: From Greek apokalypsis 'unveiling': it borrows the imagery of a final world-ending revelation, a much larger claim.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 apokalypsis「揭开」：借用世界终结式启示的意象，语气比 catastrophic 大得多。

entries.definition: A rare adjective built directly on catastrophe with -al; it exists but is far less common than catastrophic.
entries.definitionCN: 直接由 catastrophe 加 -al 构成的罕用形容词，存在但远不如 catastrophic 常用。

entries.definition: From Latin fatum 'fate': it means causing death or doom, and says nothing about the size of the loss.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 fatum「命运」：指致死或注定失败，不涉及损失规模。

entries.definition: The plainer adjective from disaster; it can describe a merely bad dinner, which catastrophic rarely does.
entries.definitionCN: 由 disaster 来的更日常的形容词，可以形容一顿很糟的晚餐，而 catastrophic 很少这样用。

entries.definition: From Latin devastare 'to lay waste': it stresses the sweeping destruction of an area or a person's feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 devastare「荒废」：强调对地区或人的情感造成的横扫式破坏。

entries.definition: From Latin ruina 'a falling down': it points at collapse, especially of finances, and is more formal and literary.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 ruina「倒塌」：指向崩塌，尤指财务，语气更正式、更书面。

entries.definition: From Latin calamitas 'loss': it emphasises the distress borne by people rather than the mechanism of the disaster.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 calamitas「损失」：强调人们承受的苦难，而非灾害的机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real set phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The base is catastrophe, a turning down; -ic makes it an adjective of that overturning.
normal.cn: 词基是 catastrophe「向下翻转」，-ic 使其成为表示该翻转的形容词。

normal.en: The -ic ending is the same one in dramatic, poetic and historic.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ic 与 dramatic、poetic、historic 中的 -ic 相同。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the professional uses: catastrophic failure, catastrophic illness, catastrophic loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出专业用法：灾难性故障、重大疾病、灾难性损失。

normal.en: The adverb is catastrophically, as in catastrophically wrong.
normal.cn: 副词是 catastrophically，如错得灾难性地。

normal.en: Geology pairs it with catastrophism, the doctrine of sudden upheaval.
normal.cn: 地质学把它与灾变论配对，后者主张突然剧变。

abstract.en: Picture a row of dominoes where the first tile is no bigger than a coin.
abstract.cn: 想象一排多米诺骨牌，第一张不过硬币大小。

abstract.en: Picture a bank statement where one line wipes out every column.
abstract.cn: 想象一张银行对账单，其中一行抹掉了所有栏目。

abstract.en: Picture a small crack that lets a whole reservoir through a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一道小裂缝，让整座水库穿墙而过。

examples.en: A single missed inspection can be catastrophic for a dam.
examples.cn: 一次漏检对一座大坝可能是灾难性的。

examples.en: The company called the recall catastrophic but kept its factories open.
examples.cn: 公司称这次召回是灾难性的，却仍让工厂开工。

examples.en: Catastrophic eruptions are rare, which is why their traces are so clear.
examples.cn: 灾难性的火山喷发很罕见，正因此留下的痕迹格外清晰。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cat（猫）+ astro（星）+ phic」——灾星压顶，连锁全毁 → 灾难性的

root: 希腊 katastrophē「翻转」（kata- 向下 + strephein 转）加希腊形容词词尾 -ikos，经拉丁 -icus 与法语 -ique 进入英语 -ic；strephein 更深来源不确定。英语 catastrophic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight meanings follow one adjective: ruin by physical force, ruin by failed planning, ruin by cost, then the stage reversal, the sudden earth change, the medical threshold, the mathematical jump and finally ordinary exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：物理力量的毁灭、谋划失败造成的毁灭、代价造成的毁灭，再到舞台逆转、地球突变、医学门槛、数学跳变，最后是日常的夸张用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one touch sends a whole row down and breaks the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：轻轻一触，整排倒下，地板被砸穿。

branches.en: SCALE AND COST: physical ruin and financial ruin are both measured by how much cannot be recovered.
branches.cn: 规模与代价：物理毁灭与财务毁灭，都以「有多少无法挽回」来衡量。

branches.en: JUDGEMENT: when nothing physical breaks, the word becomes a verdict on a decision.
branches.cn: 评判：没有实物破碎时，这个词就成了对某项决定的判词。

branches.en: FINAL JUMPS: the drama's last reversal and the model's fold are both irreversible jumps.
branches.cn: 终结性跳变：戏剧的最后逆转与模型的折点，都是不可逆的跳变。

branches.en: EARTH SCALE: geology applies the adjective to change that arrives as an event, not a trend.
branches.cn: 地球尺度：地质学把这个形容词用于「以事件形式到来」而非趋势性的变化。

branches.en: MEDICAL THRESHOLD: an illness becomes catastrophic when cost and permanence cross a line.
branches.cn: 医学门槛：当费用与不可逆性越线，疾病便成为「灾难性」的。

intro.en: The word is transparent: a Greek-derived noun plus the Greek-Latin adjective ending -ic, and both parts recur across English.
intro.cn: 这个词很透明：一个源自希腊语的名词加希腊—拉丁形容词词尾 -ic，两部分在英语中都反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Greek strophe and the prefix kata- build catastrophe and cataclysm; Latin -icus gives the English ending -ic, as in historic and dramatic.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 strophe 与前缀 kata- 构成 catastrophe 与 cataclysm；拉丁 -icus 给出英语词尾 -ic，如 historic 与 dramatic。

definition_zh: 遗忘；忘记；疏漏
definition_en: the loss of something from memory, or the act of failing to keep it in mind
core_image: 一块写满字的石板被雨水一遍遍冲刷，笔画从边缘开始变淡；旁边一把钥匙留在门内的桌上，主人已经走远。
scene: 雨夜里，写满字的石板被雨水一遍遍冲刷，靠边的笔画先淡下去，中间的字还留着，主人却已经想不起自己写过什么。 Forgetting began at the edges and took the middle last.
sceneCN: 这里指记忆内容逐渐失去、变得无法提取（第 1 个义项：遗忘）；句意为遗忘从边缘开始，最后才吞掉中间。

pos.zh: 遗忘；忘记；疏忽（不可数，指过程；可数时指具体的遗忘事例）

derivatives.zh: 忘记；遗忘（基础词加表「离开、错失」的古英语前缀，再加表「抓住」的动词，由「抓不住」转指「记不住」）
健忘的（加表「充满」的形容词词尾，由「忘记」转指「易于忘记」）
健忘地（加副词词尾，由形容词转指行为方式）
难忘的（加表否定与「能够」的两重成分，由「被忘记」转指「不可能被忘记」）
健忘（加表性质的名词词尾，由形容词转指该性质）

senses.title: Loss of what was in memory
senses.definition: the state or process in which something once known can no longer be brought to mind
senses.definitionCN: 曾知道的事物不再能被带回意识的状态或过程
senses.example: Forgetting began at the edges and took the middle last.
senses.exampleCN: 遗忘从边缘开始，最后才吞掉中间。
senses.why: The core is a lost grip: what was once held in mind is no longer held.
senses.whyCN: 核心是失去把握：曾经握在心里的东西不再被握住。

senses.title: The measured decay of retention
senses.definition: in psychology, the decline of what can be reproduced after learning, often plotted against time
senses.definitionCN: 心理学指学习后可复现内容的下降，常按时间画成曲线
senses.example: The forgetting curve fell steeply in the first hour.
senses.exampleCN: 遗忘曲线在第一个小时里陡降。
senses.why: Laboratory work turned a common experience into a measurable quantity, and the noun followed the graph.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作把共同的经验变成可测量的量，名词便跟着那条曲线走。

senses.title: Deliberate putting out of mind
senses.definition: the conscious decision to stop dwelling on something, often a wrong or a loss
senses.definitionCN: 有意决定不再纠缠某事，常指过错或损失
senses.example: Her forgetting of the insult was a decision, not a failure.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那次侮辱的遗忘是一个决定，而不是失灵。
senses.why: The word can name an act of will, which is why forgiveness and forgetting are so often paired.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指意志的动作，所以宽恕与遗忘常被并提。

senses.title: Neglect of a duty
senses.definition: the failure to attend to something one was obliged to remember
senses.definitionCN: 未能顾及本应记得的事
senses.example: The forgetting of the safety check was reported as a fault.
senses.exampleCN: 漏掉安全检查被记为一次过失。
senses.why: A duty one was bound to keep in mind is dropped, so the failure counts as negligence rather than as memory loss.
senses.whyCN: 本应记在心上的职责被丢掉，于是这种失灵算疏忽，而不算记忆丧失。

senses.title: Leaving something behind
senses.definition: the accidental failure to take something one meant to bring
senses.definitionCN: 本打算带走却意外没带
senses.example: The forgetting of the keys cost them an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 忘带钥匙让他们损失了一小时。
senses.why: The object is lost not from memory but from the hand, and the same word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 物件不是从记忆里丢失，而是从手上丢失，同一个词兼指两者。

senses.title: Losing oneself
senses.definition: the failure to keep one's own conduct in mind, as in losing restraint
senses.definitionCN: 未能看住自己的举止，如失去节制
senses.example: In the noise of the crowd there was a general forgetting of manners.
senses.exampleCN: 在人声鼎沸中，众人一时忘了礼节。
senses.why: What is forgotten here is one's own restraint, the object of the verb being the self.
senses.whyCN: 这里被忘记的是自己的节制，动词的对象就是自身。

senses.title: Erasure from the record
senses.definition: the dropping of an event or a person from written or public memory
senses.definitionCN: 把某个事件或某个人从书面或公共记忆中删去
senses.example: The forgetting of the treaty in later chronicles was deliberate.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的编年史对这条约的遗忘是有意的。
senses.why: Written memory can be edited, so an event can be forgotten by a record rather than by a person.
senses.whyCN: 书面记忆可以被编辑，因此一个事件能被记录而非被人遗忘。

senses.title: Useful dropping of the outdated
senses.titleCN: 对过时信息的有效舍弃
senses.definition: the adaptive discarding of information that no longer helps, so that newer material can be used
senses.definitionCN: 主动舍弃不再有用的信息，以便使用更新的材料
senses.example: Some forgetting is useful: old passwords only get in the way.
senses.exampleCN: 有些遗忘是有益的：旧密码只会碍事。
senses.why: Modern psychology treats the noun as neutral and sometimes as a virtue, against the older view of it as pure loss.
senses.whyCN: 现代心理学把这个名词看作中性，有时甚至是优点，与旧看法视之为纯粹损失相反。

intro.en: Forgetting is the Old English verb forgietan plus the noun suffix -ing. The verb joins a prefix of loss to a verb of grasping, and there is no Latin element. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: forgetting 是古英语动词 forgietan 加表动作的名词词尾构成。这个动词把表「失去」的前缀加在一个表「抓住」的动词上，词中不含拉丁成分。年代均为约数。

items.en: The prefix for- meant 'away, amiss, wrongly', and in many verbs it marked loss or destruction, as it still does in forbid and forlorn.
items.cn: 表「离开、错失、错误」的前缀在许多动词中标记失去或毁坏，在「禁止」与「被遗弃的」两个词中至今可见。

items.en: Gietan meant 'to grasp, seize', and it is related to the modern verb get. Its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: gietan 意为「抓住、握取」，与现代动词 get 相关。其更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: For- plus gietan produced forgietan 'to lose from the mind, fail to keep', literally to lose one's grasp on something.
items.cn: 表「失去」的前缀加 gietan 构成 forgietan「从心中失去、未能保住」，字面是「失去对某物的把握」。

items.en: The noun forgetting is recorded in Middle English, naming both the failure to remember and the state of having lost something from mind.
items.cn: 名词 forgetting 在中古英语中已有记录，既指未能记住，也指已从心中失去的状态。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the noun was used in experiments on retention, and the forgetting curve became a standard term.
items.cn: 从十九世纪晚期起，这个名词被用于保持量的实验，遗忘曲线成为标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Germanic source of gietan is not established, and no exact first citation is recorded for the noun.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：gietan 在日耳曼语之前的来源未得到证明；这个名词没有确切的最早书证。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same native verb of losing one's grasp; group two holds near neighbours of memory loss and of neglect.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「失去把握」这一本族动词的词；第二组是记忆丧失与疏忽两路的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb for losing something from mind or leaving it behind; the noun names the process or the instance.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某事从心中失去或落在别处的动词；名词指该过程或具体事例。

entries.definition: An adjective for a person who often forgets; it describes a habit, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 形容经常忘记的人；描述习惯，而非事件。

entries.definition: An adjective for what cannot be forgotten, usually because it was striking; it is the direct opposite of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 形容无法被忘记者，通常因其震撼；与名词正好相反。

entries.definition: Built from the same prefix of loss but on a verb meaning 'to give', so it means to give up a claim against someone; it is not a relative of forget at the root.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一个表「失去」的前缀加一个表「给」的动词构成，意为放弃对某人的追究；词根上与 forget 并非同族。

entries.definition: A brief failure of memory or of attention, as in a lapse of concentration; it names the slip, not the long process.
entries.definitionCN: 指记忆或注意的短暂失误，如注意力的一时松懈；指那次失误，而非长期过程。

entries.definition: The medical term for loss of memory caused by injury or illness; it is a condition, while forgetting is an everyday process.
entries.definitionCN: 指因损伤或疾病造成记忆丧失的医学名词；它是一种病症，而遗忘是日常过程。

entries.definition: The act of leaving something out, often deliberately, as in an omission from a report; it need not involve memory at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物遗漏，常为有意，如报告中漏掉一项；完全可以与记忆无关。

entries.definition: The failure to give proper attention to a duty or a person; it is broader than forgetting and need not be caused by memory.
entries.definitionCN: 指未对职责或人给予应有照料；比遗忘更宽，且不必由记忆造成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: A prefix of loss on a verb of grasping: literally to lose one's grip on something.
normal.cn: 表「失去」的前缀加表「抓住」的动词：字面就是失去对某物的把握。

normal.en: The family runs forget, forgetful, forgetfulness and unforgettable; forgive shares the prefix but not the root.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 forget、forgetful、forgetfulness、unforgettable；forgive 共用前缀却不共词根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases place the word in science and in life: the forgetting curve, deliberate forgetting, the forgetting of a name.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把词放进科学与生活：遗忘曲线、刻意遗忘、忘记一个名字。

normal.en: The noun is neutral in psychology, where some forgetting is useful, and negative in ordinary speech, where it is a fault.
normal.cn: 这个名词在心理学中是中性的，有些遗忘甚至有益；在日常说法中则是负面的，视为过失。

normal.en: The word has no Latin layer, so every attempt to read it as a Latin derivative is a false lead.
normal.cn: 这个词没有拉丁层，凡把它读作拉丁派生词的做法都是歧路。

abstract.en: Picture a slate washed by rain from the edges inward.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板被雨从边缘往里冲刷。

abstract.en: Picture keys left on a table inside a room already locked.
abstract.cn: 想象钥匙留在已经锁上的屋里桌上。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer cleared of old passwords so the new one fits.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉清掉旧密码，才放得下新的。

examples.en: Forgetting is fastest in the first hours after learning.
examples.cn: 遗忘在学习之后的头几个小时里最快。

examples.en: The forgetting of her name at the reception embarrassed him.
examples.cn: 在招待会上忘了她的名字，让他很尴尬。

examples.en: Some forgetting keeps a mind from drowning in detail.
examples.cn: 有些遗忘使头脑不致淹没在细节里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「失去」+「抓住」——抓不住了，就是忘了；记不住、落下东西、疏忽职责，都是同一次松手。

root: 古英语 forgietan「从心中失去」= 表「离开、错失」的前缀 + gietan「抓住、握取」，gietan 与现代动词 get 相关，其更深来源未得到证明。词中无拉丁成分。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one failure: a grip is lost. Lost from memory it is forgetting; lost in a measured curve it is a laboratory quantity; given up on purpose it is a decision; lost along with a duty, a pair of keys or one's manners it becomes negligence; lost from the record it is erasure; and dropped because it no longer helps it becomes useful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次失灵展开：把握失去了。从记忆里失去是遗忘；在可测曲线里失去是一个实验量；有意放弃是一个决定；连同职责、钥匙或礼节一起失去便成为疏忽；从记录里失去是被抹去；因不再有用而丢掉，则成了有益之举。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slate washed by rain from the edges inward, and keys left on a table in a locked room.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块被雨从边缘往里冲刷的石板，与留在已锁房间桌上的钥匙。

branches.en: LOSS AND ITS GRAPH: the plain failure, and the same failure counted against time.
branches.cn: 失去与它的曲线：素朴的失灵，与把同一次失灵按时间计数。

branches.en: THE DECISION NOT TO DWELL: forgetting chosen rather than suffered.
branches.cn: 不再纠缠的决定：被选择而非被遭受的遗忘。

branches.en: MISSED AND LEFT: a duty not attended to, and a thing not carried away.
branches.cn: 漏掉与落下：未被顾及的职责，与未被带走的物件。

branches.en: CONDUCT FORGOTTEN: restraint itself drops out of mind.
branches.cn: 忘了举止：连节制也从心中滑落。

branches.en: TWO ERASURES: an event struck from the record, and an old detail cleared to make room.
branches.cn: 两种抹除：被从记录中删去的事件，与被清掉以腾出位置的旧细节。

intro.en: Forgetting is native English: a prefix of loss, a verb of grasping, and a suffix of action.
intro.cn: forgetting 是纯英语本族词：表「失去」的前缀、表「抓住」的动词，加表动作的后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element here, so the Latin list is left empty; the older strata are Old English only.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不含拉丁成分，因此拉丁条目留空；更早的层次纯属古英语。

items.structure: for- (Old English prefix of loss or wrongness)
items.example: The prefix marks a failure rather than a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记失败，而非方向。

items.structure: gietan (Old English verb, strong class five)
items.example: The verb is the ancestor of modern get.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是现代 get 的祖先。

items.example: The compound turned a grasp into a losing of hold.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把「抓握」变成「失去把握」。

items.meaning: to fail to remember or to bring
items.example: I forget the address every winter.
items.exampleCN: 每年冬天我都忘记那个地址。

items.meaning: the losing of a grip on memory
items.example: Forgetting is not always a fault.

items.exampleCN: 健忘在这个家里代代都有。

items.example: The view from the ridge was unforgettable.
items.exampleCN: 山脊上的景色令人难忘。

definition_zh: 敏捷；乐意；欣然
definition_en: brisk and cheerful readiness to do something
core_image: 一声令下立刻起跑的猎犬：腿快，心也快
scene: 教练刚喊完集合，他已经穿好钉鞋站在跑道上了。 She accepted the extra assignment with alacrity.
sceneCN: 这里 alacrity 是「乐意、欣然」（第 2 个义项：愉快而敏捷的响应）；句意是她欣然接受了额外的任务。

pos.zh: 敏捷；欣然；爽快的意愿

derivatives.zh: alacrity 的形容词形式（罕用），义为「敏捷的；乐意的」
同源结构的姊妹词，来自拉丁 celeritas 加 -ity，义为「迅速；敏捷」（词源相关，非同根）

senses.title: Briskness of movement or response
senses.definition: quick, lively speed in acting or answering
senses.definitionCN: 行动或应答的迅捷与活泼
senses.example: The dog sprang up with alacrity at the whistle.
senses.exampleCN: 哨声一响，狗立刻敏捷地跳起来。
senses.why: The Latin base alacer meant lively and quick, so the noun first names physical briskness.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 alacer 意为「活泼敏捷」，名词最初便指动作上的麻利。

senses.title: Cheerful readiness of mind
senses.definition: eagerness and willingness, a cheerful promptness to agree or comply
senses.definitionCN: 热切的自愿，愉快爽快地答应或顺从
senses.example: He accepted the invitation with alacrity.
senses.exampleCN: 他欣然接受了邀请。
senses.why: A lively spirit is also a willing one, so the quickness of the body widened into eagerness of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 活泼的精神也是愿意的精神，身体的敏捷便扩展为心灵的踊跃。

intro.en: From a Latin adjective meaning lively, kept almost unchanged in form by English.
intro.cn: 来自一个意为「活泼」的拉丁形容词，英语几乎原样保留了它的形态。

items.en: A reconstructed root *h₂el- expressed movement, energy, or nourishment; the exact line is uncertain.
items.cn: 重构词根 *h₂el- 或与运动、能量、滋养相关，具体路径不确定。

items.en: alacer meant lively, brisk, and eager, applied to both bodies and minds.
items.cn: 拉丁语 alacer 意为「活泼、敏捷、热切」，可形容身体与心神。

items.en: alacritas named liveliness and eagerness as a quality.
items.cn: alacritas 指「活泼、踊跃」这一品质。

items.en: English took alacritas directly as alacrity, first with the Latin sense of liveliness.
items.cn: 15 世纪英语直接借入 alacritas 作 alacrity，最初保留「活泼」义。

items.en: Today the word almost always means cheerful willingness, usually after with.
items.cn: 现代英语中该词几乎总指「欣然乐意」，常与 with 连用。

note.en: The first group holds a rare sibling word and an unrelated look-alike; the second holds words for eagerness.
note.cn: 第一组收一个罕用同族词与一个无关的形近词；第二组收表示「热切」的词。

entries.definition: a rare adjective form meaning lively and willing
entries.definitionCN: 罕用形容词，意为「活泼乐意的」

entries.definition: a set phrase using the noun itself
entries.definitionCN: 使用该名词的固定说法「精神的踊跃」

entries.definition: bold daring; only looks and sounds similar, different root
entries.definitionCN: 大胆放肆；仅形音相近，词源不同

entries.definition: keen desire to do or have something
entries.definitionCN: 渴望；热切

entries.definition: willingness to act at once
entries.definitionCN: 愿意；随时准备行动

entries.definition: the quality of acting quickly and without delay
entries.definitionCN: 迅速；果断

entries.definition: the state of being glad to comply
entries.definitionCN: 自愿；乐意

entries.definition: intense enjoyment and interest, stronger and warmer than brisk readiness
entries.definitionCN: 热情；兴致，比爽快应允更炽热

normalIntro.en: From Latin alacer, lively: a mind that jumps up like a quick dog.
normalIntro.cn: 来自拉丁语 alacer「活泼」：一颗像灵犬一样立刻起跳的心。

normal.en: with alacrity is the classic exam phrase.
normal.cn: with alacrity 是考试经典搭配。

normal.en: alacer meant lively; alacrity keeps the bounce.
normal.cn: alacer 意为活泼，alacrity 保留了那份弹跳感。

normal.en: It combines speed and gladness in one word.
normal.cn: 它把「快」与「乐」合在一个词里。

normal.en: People accept invitations with alacrity, not reluctance.
normal.cn: 人们欣然受邀，而不是勉为其难。

normal.en: Compare audacity, daring, a different word that merely looks alike.
normal.cn: 对比 audacity「大胆」，只是形近而已。

abstract.en: Picture a dog already running before the whistle ends.
abstract.cn: 想象哨声未落，狗已经跑出去了。

abstract.en: See a hand shooting up before the teacher finishes the question.
abstract.cn: 想象老师问题还没问完，一只手已经举起。

abstract.en: Imagine the sound of eager feet on stairs going up two at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象上楼时一步两级的热切脚步声。

examples.en: She agreed to help with unfeigned alacrity.
examples.cn: 她毫不做作地欣然答应帮忙。

examples.en: The troops moved with alacrity when the order came.
examples.cn: 命令一到，部队闻令即动。

examples.en: He volunteered with alacrity for the hardest task.
examples.cn: 他踊跃请缨承担最艰巨的任务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿拉渴力」——阿拉（我们）渴了也有力气，一喊就来，干劲十足。

root: 拉丁语 alacer「活泼敏捷的」派生名词 alacritas「踊跃」，15 世纪直接借入英语作 alacrity；更早词基可溯至重构形式 *h₂el-，存疑。本义为身体敏捷，现代常用义转为心甘情愿的爽快。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses split one lively energy: quickness of the limbs, then gladness of the will.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项把同一种活泼的能量一分为二：一是手脚的麻利，二是心意的甘愿。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dog already running before the whistle finishes.
core.cn: 核心意象：哨声未落，狗已飞奔而出。

branches.en: a whistled command answered in mid-air
branches.cn: 哨令未完已腾空而起的应答

branches.en: sailors running up the rigging at once
branches.cn: 水手们即刻攀上索具

branches.en: an acceptance letter sent back the same afternoon
branches.cn: 当天下午就寄回的应允信

branches.en: volunteering for the hardest job before it is described
branches.cn: 任务还没讲完就踊跃请缨

branches.en: one eager energy, in the legs and in the heart
branches.cn: 同一股热望，在腿上，也在心里

intro.en: A Latin adjective of liveliness with its noun ending, borrowed whole.
intro.cn: 一个表示「活泼」的拉丁形容词连其名词词尾被整体借入。

latinIntro.en: alacer and alacritas are recorded Latin forms.
latinIntro.cn: alacer 与 alacritas 都是有记录的拉丁形态。

definition_zh: n. 弧，弧线；电弧；（故事或人生的）发展轨迹　v. 呈弧形移动；形成电弧
definition_en: A curved line or path, like part of a circle; a bright electric discharge across a gap; the shape of a story or career as it rises and falls; as a verb, to move in a curve.
core_image: 弯过来的一段线，从这头连到那头
scene: 球在空中划出一道长长的弧线。 The ball traced a long arc across the sky.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arc 指弯曲的一段线或路径，形状像圆的一部分。

pos.zh: 弧；弧线；电弧；发展轨迹
呈弧形移动；形成电弧

senses.title: A curved line or path
senses.definition: a part of a circle or other curve, or the curved path a moving object follows
senses.definitionCN: 圆或其他曲线的一段，或运动物体所走的弯曲路径
senses.example: The lamp threw an arc of light on the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 灯在墙上投出一道弧形的光。
senses.why: Latin arcus meant a bow, and a bent bow is exactly this shape, so every sense keeps that single bend.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，拉开的弓正是这个形状，所以各个义项都保留着那一道弯。

senses.title: A bright electric discharge
senses.definition: a luminous bridge of current jumping across a gap between two electrodes, used in welding and old lamps
senses.definitionCN: 电流跨过两个电极间隙形成的发光桥，用于焊接与早期灯具
senses.example: An arc jumped between the two worn contacts.
senses.exampleCN: 两个磨损的触点之间跳起了电弧。
senses.why: The discharge bends like a bow between the terminals, so the shape word was borrowed for the phenomenon.
senses.whyCN: 放电在两端之间弯成弓形，于是这个表形状的词被借来指这一现象。

senses.title: The shape of a story
senses.definition: the course a narrative, character or career takes as it rises, turns and resolves
senses.definitionCN: 叙事、人物或事业在上升、转折与收束中所走的历程
senses.example: The novel gives every minor character a full arc.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说给每个配角都安排了完整的发展线。
senses.why: Plot drawn on paper looks like a rising and falling curve, so the geometry word became a term for narrative shape.
senses.whyCN: 把情节画在纸上就是一条起落的曲线，于是这个几何词变成了叙事结构的术语。

senses.title: To move in a curve
senses.definition: of a moving thing, to travel along a curved path rather than a straight one
senses.definitionCN: 指运动之物沿弯曲路径而非直线行进
senses.example: The gull arced low over the water and turned back.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥贴着水面划了个弧又折回来。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb with no change of shape: the path becomes the action of following that path.
senses.whyCN: 名词不变形就转为动词：路径本身变成了「走这条路径」的动作。

intro.en: Arc is Latin arcus, a bow or arch, from an ancient root meaning bow. English took it through Old French arc as a geometry term, then extended it to electricity and to stories.
intro.cn: arc 就是拉丁语 arcus「弓、拱」，出自一个意为「弓」的古老词根。英语经古法语 arc 作为几何术语吸收，后来扩展到电学与叙事。

items.en: The reconstructed root arkw- meant bow, the bent weapon that gave the whole family its shape.
items.cn: 重构词根 arkw- 意为「弓」，这件弯曲的武器给整个词族提供了形状。

items.en: Latin arcus meant a bow, and by extension any arch or curve, including the rainbow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arcus 意为「弓」，引申指任何拱或曲线，也包括彩虹。

items.en: Old French arc kept both bow and curve, and passed the geometrical sense to English.
items.cn: 古法语 arc 兼指弓与曲线，并把几何义传给英语。

items.en: English recorded arc in the late fourteenth century for a segment of a circle or curve.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪末记录 arc，指圆或曲线的一段。

items.en: Humphry Davy demonstrated the electric arc in the early nineteenth century, and the bow-shaped flame kept the name.
items.cn: 戴维在 19 世纪初演示了电弧，那道弓形的火焰沿用了这个名字。

items.en: Twentieth-century film and television criticism made story arc a standard term for a plotted course.
items.cn: 20 世纪影视批评把 story arc 变成指情节历程的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against ark, which sounds identical, and arcane, which has a different root; the near-meaning group lists other words for a bend.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与同音的 ark、以及词根不同的 arcane 混淆；近义组列出其他表示「弯」的词。

entries.definition: A curved structure over an opening.
entries.definitionCN: 洞口上方的弧形结构。

entries.definition: A large boat, as in Noah's ark.
entries.definitionCN: 大船，如诺亚方舟。

entries.definition: A row of arches; a games hall.
entries.definitionCN: 一排拱；街机游戏厅。

entries.definition: Known only to a few; mysterious.
entries.definitionCN: 只有少数人知道的；神秘的。

entries.definition: A smoothly bending line.
entries.definitionCN: 平滑弯曲的线。

entries.definition: A bent weapon for arrows.
entries.definitionCN: 射箭的弯弓。

entries.definition: The curved shape of a new moon.
entries.definitionCN: 新月的弯形。

entries.definition: The path of a flying object.
entries.definitionCN: 飞行物体的路径。

normalIntro.en: Arc is the bow shape: a bent line, a bent flame, a bent plot, or the act of bending through the air.
normalIntro.cn: arc 就是弓的形状：弯的线、弯的火焰、弯的情节，或在空中弯过去的动作。

normal.en: Arc and arch share the root, but arch is a structure.
normal.cn: arc 与 arch 同根，但 arch 指建筑结构。

normal.en: The verb forms are arced and arcing, with no k.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 arced 与 arcing，不加 k。

normal.en: Story arc is the fixed term in film and fiction.
normal.cn: story arc 是影视与小说的固定术语。

normal.en: Arc sounds like ark, but ark means a boat.
normal.cn: arc 与 ark 同音，但 ark 指船。

normal.en: Arcane looks related but comes from a different root.
normal.cn: arcane 看似相关，其实词根不同。

abstract.en: Picture a drawn bow held still.
abstract.cn: 想象一张拉开后静止的弓。

abstract.en: Imagine a ball writing a curve on the sky.
abstract.cn: 想象球在天上写出一道曲线。

abstract.en: Think of a plot drawn as a hill on paper.
abstract.cn: 想象情节被画成纸上一座小山。

examples.en: The road makes a wide arc around the lake.
examples.cn: 公路绕着湖划出一道大弧。

examples.en: Sparks arced between the loose wires.
examples.cn: 松脱的电线之间迸出弧形火花。

examples.en: Her career follows an unusual arc.
examples.cn: 她的职业生涯走出一条不寻常的轨迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arc 与 arch 同根，拉丁 arcus「弓」——弓弯出来的那段线，就是弧 arc。

root: 原始印欧词根 arkw-「弓」生出拉丁 arcus「弓、拱」，经古法语 arc 进入英语指弧；19 世纪因放电呈弓形而指电弧，20 世纪又借指故事的发展轨迹。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are one bend: a bent line, a bent flame, a bent plot, and the act of moving along a bend.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一道弯：弯的线、弯的火焰、弯的情节，以及沿着弯走过去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one bent line running from this end to that
core.cn: 核心意象：弯过来的一段线，从这头连到那头

branches.en: A lamp writing light on a wall.
branches.cn: 灯在墙上写出一道光弧。

branches.en: A flame jumping between contacts.
branches.cn: 触点之间跳起的火焰。

branches.en: A plot rising, turning, resolving.
branches.cn: 上升、转折、收束的情节。

branches.en: A gull bending low over water.
branches.cn: 贴着水面弯过去的海鸥。

branches.en: Both are curves you can draw.
branches.cn: 两者都是能画出来的曲线。

intro.en: Arc is the bow root itself, and with -ade and -er it builds arcade and archer; arch is the same root through French.
intro.cn: arc 本身就是「弓」词根，加 -ade 与 -er 构成 arcade 与 archer；arch 是同一词根经法语而来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arcus, a bow, and curvus, bent, which gives curve and curvature.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arcus「弓」与 curvus「弯的」，后者产生 curve 与 curvature。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arcus 产生 arc 与 arch。
古法语 arc 传入英语。

definition_zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇（信心、权威）
definition_en: to weaken something gradually from below, often secretly, by taking away what supports it
core_image: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看上去完好，根基却已经空了
scene: 老墙脚下，水从砖缝里一点点掏空泥沙，墙面看着完好，根基却已经空了。 Constant leaks had begun to undermine the old wall.
sceneCN: 这里指从根基上逐渐削弱、掏空（第 1 个义项：损毁实物的基础）；句意为持续的渗漏已经开始逐渐损毁那面老墙。

pos.zh: 削弱；暗中破坏；逐渐损毁根基；动摇

derivatives.zh: 由该动词的现在分词转成的名词或形容词，义为「暗中破坏；起削弱作用的」
由该动词加表示施动者的名词尾构成，义为「暗中破坏者」
由该动词的过去分词转成的形容词，义为「已被削弱的；根基受损的」

senses.title: Hollow out a physical base
senses.definition: of water, digging or decay, to remove the material under a wall, road or building
senses.definitionCN: 指水、挖掘或腐朽移除墙、路或建筑底下的材料
senses.example: Salt water can undermine the foundation of a bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 盐水会逐渐掏空桥基。
senses.why: The word is literally under plus mine, so the first sense is the mining sense: taking the ground out from beneath a structure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上就是「在下」加「挖掘」，所以第一个义项就是采矿义：把结构底下的地基取走。

senses.title: Secretly damage a plan or effort
senses.definition: to weaken a plan, campaign or effort by quiet action rather than open opposition
senses.definitionCN: 以暗中行动而非公开反对来削弱计划、行动或努力
senses.example: A few leaks were enough to undermine the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 几次泄密就足以破坏那项计划。
senses.why: A tunnel dug under a defence does its work unseen, and the word kept that secrecy when it moved from walls to plans.
senses.whyCN: 在防线底下挖的坑道在看不见处做工，这个词从墙转到计划时保留了那份隐秘。

senses.title: Weaken a person's confidence
senses.definition: to make someone steadily less sure of themselves or of a decision
senses.definitionCN: 使某人对自己或某个决定逐渐失去把握
senses.example: Constant criticism undermined her confidence.
senses.exampleCN: 不断的批评削弱了她的信心。
senses.why: Confidence stands on supports, and enough small attacks from below can make it sag without ever being hit directly.
senses.whyCN: 信心立在支撑上，足够多来自下方的小攻击能让它下沉，却从未被直接击中。

senses.title: Shake an authority or position
senses.definition: to make a leader, office or institution less respected and less able to act
senses.definitionCN: 使领导者、职位或机构受到的尊重减少、行动能力下降
senses.example: The scandal undermined the minister's authority.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻动摇了那位部长的权威。
senses.why: Authority is a structure that stands on accepted ground, and removing that ground is the word's exact work.
senses.whyCN: 权威是立在公认地基上的结构，而抽走那层地基正是这个词的确切工作。

senses.title: Damage a reputation
senses.definition: to lower the trust that others place in a person, company or brand
senses.definitionCN: 降低他人对个人、公司或品牌的信任
senses.example: Rumours undermined the company's reputation.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言损害了公司的声誉。
senses.why: A reputation is built from many small confirmations, so it can be undone from below without any single open attack.
senses.whyCN: 声誉由许多小确认堆成，因此可以被下方一点点拆掉，而无需任何一次公开攻击。

senses.title: Weaken an argument
senses.definition: to make a case less convincing by removing the support under one of its claims
senses.definitionCN: 抽掉某个主张底下的支撑，使论证不那么令人信服
senses.example: One weak example undermined the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 一个薄弱的例证削弱了整个论证。
senses.why: An argument is a building of reasons, and the word is used for taking a load-bearing stone out of it.
senses.whyCN: 论证是由理由搭起的建筑，这个词就用来形容从中抽走一块承重的石头。

senses.title: Dig beneath a seam or deposit
senses.definition: in mining, to cut a tunnel under a body of coal or ore so that it can be removed
senses.definitionCN: 采矿中指在煤层或矿体下方开掘巷道以便采出
senses.example: Miners undermined the seam from a lower tunnel.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工从下方的巷道掏挖那层煤层。
senses.why: This is the technical sense that keeps the two halves of the word visible: under, and mine.
senses.whyCN: 这是让词的两个半截都保持可见的技术义：在下，以及挖掘。

senses.title: Sap physical strength
senses.definition: of illness, hunger or overwork, to wear down a person's strength slowly
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病、饥饿或过劳缓慢损耗一个人的体力
senses.example: Illness had undermined his strength over the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病在冬天里一点点损耗了他的体力。
senses.why: The body also has foundations, and slow removal from below describes a decline that no single event explains.
senses.whyCN: 身体也有根基，而从下方缓慢抽走，描述的是一种无法归因于单一事件的衰退。

senses.title: Break the ground under trust
senses.definition: to make the trust between people or groups collapse through repeated small betrayals
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复的小背叛使人或群体之间的信任崩塌
senses.example: Broken promises undermined the trust between them.
senses.exampleCN: 屡次食言破坏了他们之间的信任。
senses.why: Trust rests on a floor of kept promises, and this word describes the floor being taken away one tile at a time.
senses.whyCN: 信任铺在守诺的地板上，而这个词描述的就是地板被一块块抽走。

intro.en: Undermine is an English compound of under and mine. The first half is native Old English; the second came through Old French and its deeper origin is uncertain.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语由「在下」与「矿、挖掘」构成的复合词。前半是本土古英语，后半经古法语而来，其更深来源不明。

items.en: Under is a native preposition and prefix meaning below, and it has shaped hundreds of English compounds.
items.cn: under 是本土介词与副词，意为在下方，它参与构成了数以百计的英语复合词。

items.en: The noun meant a mine, an ore bed or a subterranean passage, and English borrowed it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 这个名词意为矿、矿层或地下通道，英语在中世纪借入。

items.en: The written source is mina, but its own origin is uncertain; it may have come from a Celtic word for ore.
items.cn: 有记载的来源是 mina，但它自身的来源不明，可能来自某支凯尔特语中表示矿石的词。

items.en: The verb first meant to dig under a wall or a fort so that it would fall; the military sense is the oldest recorded one.
items.cn: 这个动词最初意为在墙或堡垒底下挖掘使之倒塌；军事义是最早有记载的义项。

items.en: From digging under defences the word moved to weakening confidence, authority and trust; the date of each shift is uncertain.
items.cn: 从在防线底下挖掘，这个词转向削弱信心、权威与信任；每次转变的年代不确定。

items.en: Medicine uses it for slow declines of strength and immunity that no single cause can explain.
items.cn: 医学用它形容无法归因于单一原因的体力与免疫力缓慢衰退。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like undermine; the second group names neighbouring ways of weakening something.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与 undermine 相近；第二组是与「削弱、破坏」意思相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The act of weakening something from below or in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 指从下方或暗中削弱某物的行为。

entries.definition: A person who quietly damages a plan or an authority.
entries.definitionCN: 指暗中破坏计划或权威的人。

entries.definition: An excavation for ore, or the act of digging one; the second half of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 指矿坑，或挖掘矿坑的行为；是本词的后半部分。

entries.definition: Below the surface of the earth; it shares the prefix but not the mining verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指地面之下；共享前缀，但不含那个挖掘动词。

entries.definition: To take on a task; it shares the prefix but has an unrelated second half.
entries.definitionCN: 指承担任务；共享前缀，但后半部分无关。

entries.definition: To make less strong; the broad word, with no image of digging or secrecy.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变弱；最宽泛的词，不含挖掘或隐秘的意象。

entries.definition: To wear something away gradually by wind, water or friction; it stresses slow surface loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指风、水或摩擦逐渐磨损；强调表面的缓慢流失。

entries.definition: To damage something deliberately, usually from inside an organisation; it stresses intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指故意破坏，通常从组织内部下手；强调意图。

entries.definition: To overturn an authority or system from within; it stresses turning the order upside down.
entries.definitionCN: 指从内部颠覆权威或制度；强调把秩序翻过来。

entries.definition: To reduce the function of something; it stresses loss of working ability rather than support.
entries.definitionCN: 指降低某物的功能；强调工作能力的损失，而非支撑。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two visible halves, under and mine, and the image of ground removed from beneath.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想利用两个看得见的半截——「在下」与「挖掘」，以及从底下抽走地面的意象。

normal.en: Say the two halves in order: under, then mine. The word is a tunnel dug beneath a wall.
normal.cn: 按顺序念两个半截：先「在下」，再「挖掘」。这个词就是在墙底下挖的一条坑道。

normal.en: A wall can look perfect from the street while the ground beneath it has already been taken away.
normal.cn: 一面墙从街上看似完好，它底下的土却早已被掏走。

normal.en: A rumour works like water in a brick joint: no hammer, but the joint gets wider.
normal.cn: 谣言像砖缝里的水：没有锤子，缝却越来越宽。

normal.en: The word is always gradual; it never means one clean blow.
normal.cn: 这个词总是渐进的，从不指干净利落的一击。

normal.en: The secret is part of the meaning: the damage is done where no one is looking.
normal.cn: 隐秘是意义的一部分：破坏发生在没人看的地方。

abstract.en: Undermining is the quiet form of opposition, and it is harder to answer than an open attack.
abstract.cn: 暗中破坏是反对的安静形式，比公开攻击更难回应。

abstract.en: Structures fail from below long before they fail from the front.
abstract.cn: 结构从下方失效，远早于它从正面失效。

abstract.en: What is undermined is not destroyed but left standing on nothing.
abstract.cn: 被掏空的东西不是被摧毁，而是被留在虚无之上继续立着。

examples.en: The constant flooding undermined the road's foundations.
examples.cn: 反复的洪水损毁了那条路的地基。

examples.en: His careless remarks undermined the peace talks.
examples.cn: 他轻率的言论破坏了和谈。

examples.en: Low pay undermines the morale of the whole team.
examples.cn: 低薪削弱了整个团队的士气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安德曼」——「安德」是「在下」，在墙「曼」慢地挖，墙就从底下空了：暗中削弱

root: 古英语 under「在下」+ 古法语 mine「矿、挖掘」→ 中古英语 undermine「在墙下挖坑道使之倒塌」→ 现代义「从根基上逐渐削弱、暗中破坏」；其中「矿」的更深来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one direction, from below and often unseen: a foundation, a plan, a confidence, an authority, a reputation, an argument, a coal seam, a body and the trust between people.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项保持同一个方向——自下而上、常在暗处：地基、计划、信心、权威、声誉、论证、煤层、身体，以及人与人之间的信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water taking sand out of a brick joint until the wall stands on emptiness.
core.cn: 核心意象：水把砖缝里的沙一点点带走，直到墙立在空处。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL BASE BRANCH: water takes a bridge's foundation, and miners cut under a seam.
branches.cn: 实物根基分支：水掏空桥基，矿工在煤层下方开挖。

branches.en: THE PLAN AND ARGUMENT BRANCH: leaks damage a campaign and one weak example damages a case.
branches.cn: 计划与论证分支：泄密破坏行动，一个薄弱例证破坏论证。

branches.en: THE INNER STRENGTH BRANCH: criticism lowers confidence and illness lowers bodily strength.
branches.cn: 内在力量分支：批评压低信心，疾病损耗体力。

branches.en: THE AUTHORITY BRANCH: a scandal removes the ground a minister stands on.
branches.cn: 权威分支：丑闻抽走部长脚下的地基。

branches.en: THE REPUTATION AND TRUST BRANCH: rumours spoil a name and broken promises spoil a bond.
branches.cn: 声誉与信任分支：谣言毁掉名声，食言毁掉纽带。

intro.en: Undermine is a native prefix on a borrowed noun, and the join is so old that English speakers no longer feel the two parts separately.
intro.cn: 这是一个本土前缀加在借来的名词上，接合得太久，英语使用者已不再分别感觉这两个部分。

latinIntro.en: The second half reached English through Old French from Medieval Latin mina, a word of uncertain origin that may be Celtic.
latinIntro.cn: 后半部分经古法语、来自中世纪拉丁语 mina，这个词来源不明，可能出自凯尔特语。

items.example: It fixes the direction of the damage from the start.
items.exampleCN: 它从一开始就定下破坏的方向。

items.meaning: a pit for ore, a subterranean passage
items.example: The noun supplies the digging that the verb describes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供动词所描述的挖掘动作。

items.structure: English verb converted from the noun
items.example: English turned the pit into an action without adding an ending.
items.exampleCN: 英语把这个坑直接变成动作，没有加词尾。

items.example: It forms the noun for the slow work of weakening.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示「缓慢削弱」这一工作的名词。

items.example: It names the person who digs from below.
items.exampleCN: 它命名从下方挖掘的人。

items.example: It forms undermined, a position already weakened.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 undermined，表示已被削弱的处境。

items.meaning: the act of weakening from below
items.meaningCN: 从下方逐渐削弱的行为
items.example: The constant undermining of trust ruined the talks.
items.exampleCN: 对信任的持续侵蚀毁了会谈。

items.meaning: one who digs from below or weakens in secret
items.meaningCN: 从下方挖掘或暗中削弱的人
items.example: An underminer works out of sight.
items.exampleCN: 暗中破坏者在看不见的地方行事。
